title.zh: 卷一百四十三 列傳第三十: 馬祖常 巙巙 自當 阿榮 小雲石海涯 泰不華 余闕
title.en: Volume 143 Biographies 30: Mazuchang, Kuikui, Zidang, Arong, Xiaoyunshihaiya, Taibuhua, Yuque
title.raw: 卷一百四十三 列傳第三十: 馬祖常 巙巙 自當 阿榮 小雲石海涯 泰不華 余闕 Volume 143 Biographies 30: Mazuchang, Kuikui, Zidang, Arong, Xiaoyunshihaiya, Taibuhua, Yuque

sentences.zh: 马祖常

translations.literal: Mazuchang
translations.idiomatic: Mazuchang

sentences.zh: 马祖常，字伯庸，世为雍古部，居净州天山。

translations.literal: Mazuchang, style name Boyong, for generations of the Yonggu tribe, dwelt at Tianshan in Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mazuchang, whose style name was Boyong, came from the Yonggu tribe and lived at Tianshan in Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有锡里吉思者，于祖常为高祖，金季为凤翔兵马判官，以节死赠恆州刺史，子孙因其官，以马为氏。

translations.literal: There was one Sirigisi, who was great-grandfather to Zuchang; in the late Jin he was military affairs judge at Fengxiang and died for integrity, posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Heng Prefecture; descendants took Ma as their surname because of his office.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Sirigisi, who served in the late Jin as military affairs judge at Fengxiang, died defending his integrity and was posthumously made prefect of Heng Prefecture; later generations took the surname Ma from that office.

sentences.zh: 曾祖月合乃，从世祖征宋，留汴，掌馈饷，累官礼部尚书。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yuehenai followed the Founder in the campaign against Song, remained at Bian, managed provisions, and rose through offices to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yuehenai accompanied Kublai on the conquest of Song, stayed at Bian to manage supplies, and eventually became Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 父润，同知漳州路总管府事，家于光州。

translations.literal: His father Run was associate administrator of the Zhangzhou Circuit Pacification Commissioner's office; the family settled in Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Run served as deputy administrator of the Zhangzhou circuit and made his home in Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖常七岁知学，得钱即以市书。

translations.literal: At seven Zuchang knew how to study; whenever he obtained money he immediately used it to buy books.
translations.idiomatic: Zuchang took to learning at seven and spent every coin he could get on books.

sentences.zh: 十岁时，见烛欹烧屋，解衣沃水以灭火，咸嗟异之。

translations.literal: At ten he saw a candle tilted and burning the house; he stripped off his clothes, poured water to extinguish the fire, and all sighed in wonder at him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was ten he saw a tilted candle set the house ablaze, stripped off his clothes, soaked them in water, and put out the fire—everyone marveled at his presence of mind.

sentences.zh: 既长，益笃于学。

translations.literal: Once grown, he became still more devoted to learning.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older his devotion to study only deepened.

sentences.zh: 蜀儒张摐道仪真，往受业其门，质以疑义数十，摐甚器之。

translations.literal: The Shu scholar Zhang Peng taught the Way at Yizhen; he went to study under him, submitted several tens of doubtful points for judgment, and Peng greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Yizhen to study under the Shu scholar Zhang Peng, posed dozens of difficult questions, and won Peng's high regard.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，科举法行，乡贡、会试皆中第一，廷试为第二人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yanyou era, when the examination system was implemented, he placed first in both the provincial presentation and the metropolitan examination, and was second in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: When civil examinations were restored early in the Yanyou era, he ranked first in the provincial and metropolitan rounds and second in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 授应奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant-in-Waiting for Hanlin Documents.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an attendant-in-waiting for Hanlin documents.

sentences.zh: 拜监察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 是时仁宗在御已久，犹居东宫，饮酒常过度。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Renzong had long been on the throne yet still resided in the Eastern Palace, and often drank to excess.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Renzong had reigned for years but still lived in the Eastern Palace and often drank too much.

sentences.zh: 祖常上书请「御正衙，立朝仪，御史执简，太史执笔，则虽有怀奸利己乞官求赏者，不敢出诸口。

translations.literal: Zuchang submitted a memorial requesting: "Hold court in the main hall, establish court ritual, let censors hold their tablets and the grand astrologer keep the record—then even those harboring treachery, seeking private gain, begging offices, or asking rewards will not dare speak them aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Zuchang memorialized the throne, urging that the heir "hold court in the main hall and establish proper ceremony, with censors bearing their tablets and the grand astrologer keeping the record, so that even men plotting for private gain or begging offices and rewards would not dare speak out.

sentences.zh: 天子承天地祖宗之重，当极调摄，至于酒醴，近侍进御，当思一献百拜之义。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven bears the weight of Heaven, Earth, and the ancestors; he ought to regulate himself to the utmost; as for wine, when close attendants present it for his use, he should reflect on the meaning of one offering and a hundred bows."
translations.idiomatic: The heir bears the weight of Heaven, Earth, and the imperial ancestors and must govern himself with utmost care; when attendants offer wine, he should remember the ritual meaning of a single cup and a hundred bows."

sentences.zh: 英宗为皇太子，又上书请慎简师傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was crown prince, he again submitted a memorial requesting careful selection of tutors.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was crown prince, Zuchang submitted another memorial urging careful choice of tutors."

sentences.zh: 于是奸臣铁木迭兒为丞相，威权自恣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the treacherous minister Temuder became chief councillor and wielded power as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the corrupt minister Temuder became chief councillor and wielded power without restraint.

sentences.zh: 祖常知其盗观国史，率同列劾奏其十罪，仁宗震怒，黜罢之。

translations.literal: Zuchang knew that he had stolen and viewed the national histories; he led his colleagues in memorializing ten crimes against him; Emperor Renzong was greatly angered and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Temuder had stolen and read the national histories, Zuchang led his colleagues in impeaching him on ten counts; Renzong was furious and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 秦州山移，祖常言：「山不动之物，今而动焉，由在野有当用不用之贤，在官有当言不言之佞，故致然尔。」

translations.literal: When a mountain shifted in Qin Prefecture, Zuchang said: "Mountains are things that do not move; that one moves now is because in the wilds there are worthy men who ought to be employed but are not, and in office there are flatterers who ought to speak but do not—therefore it has come to this."
translations.idiomatic: When a mountain shifted in Qin Prefecture, Zuchang said, "Mountains are not meant to move. If one moves, it is because worthy men in retirement are not being used and flatterers in office will not speak the truth—that is what brings such omens."

sentences.zh: 疏闻，大臣皆家居待罪。

translations.literal: When the memorial was heard, the great ministers all remained at home awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the court, senior ministers all stayed home awaiting punishment.

sentences.zh: 祖常荐贤拔滞，知无不言。

translations.literal: Zuchang recommended the worthy and raised the stagnant; what he knew he did not fail to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Zuchang recommended worthy men, lifted the overlooked, and spoke out whenever he knew something needed saying.

sentences.zh: 俄改宣政院经历，月餘辞归，起为社稷署令。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to administrator of the Xuanzheng Commission; after a little more than a month he resigned and returned, then was appointed director of the Altar of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made administrator of the Xuanzheng Commission, resigned after little more than a month, and was then appointed director of the Altar of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 亡何，奸臣复相，左迁开平县尹，因欲中伤之，遂退居光州。

translations.literal: Before long the treacherous minister became chief councillor again; Zuchang was demoted to magistrate of Kaiping County; because they wished to harm him, he withdrew to reside in Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the corrupt minister returned to power; Zuchang was demoted to magistrate of Kaiping, and when enemies tried to ruin him he retired to Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，奸臣既死，乃除翰林待制。

translations.literal: After a long while, once the treacherous minister had died, he was appointed Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: After the corrupt minister died, he was appointed Hanlin academician-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 泰定建储，擢典宝少监、太子左赞善。

translations.literal: When Taiding established the heir, he was promoted to Vice-Director of the Palace Treasures and Left Assistant to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiding named an heir, he was promoted to vice-director of palace treasures and left assistant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 寻兼翰林直学士，除礼部尚书。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Hanlin Academician Expositor, then appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also served as Hanlin expositor and was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 丁祖母忧，起为右赞善，复除礼部尚书，寻辞归。

translations.literal: He mourned his grandmother; recalled from mourning he became Right Assistant to the Crown Prince, again appointed Minister of Rites, and soon resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his grandmother he was recalled as right assistant to the crown prince and again made Minister of Rites, but soon resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 天历元年，召为燕王内尉，仍入礼部，两知贡举，一为读卷官，时称得人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli he was summoned as inner commandant to the Prince of Yan, still entered the Ministry of Rites, twice supervised the examinations, once served as reader of examination papers, and at the time it was said he obtained the right men.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianli he was summoned as inner commandant to the Prince of Yan, returned to the Ministry of Rites, twice supervised the civil examinations, once served as chief reader of papers, and was praised for selecting good men.

sentences.zh: 升参议中书省事，参定亲郊礼仪，充读册祝官，拜治书侍御史，历徽政副使，迁江南行台中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to participant in the affairs of the Secretariat of the Central Secretariat, helped fix the rituals for the emperor's personal suburban sacrifice, served as reader of the prayer tablets, was appointed Associate Censor of the Secretariat, passed through Vice-Commissioner of the Huizheng Commission, and was transferred to Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to participant in Secretariat affairs, helped draft the rituals for the emperor's suburban sacrifice, read the prayer tablets, became associate censor of the Secretariat, served as vice-commissioner of the Huizheng Commission, and was transferred to censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元统元年，召议新政，赐白金二百两、钞万贯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was summoned to discuss the new policies and was granted two hundred taels of white silver and ten thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuantong he was called to discuss new policies and rewarded with two hundred taels of silver and ten thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 又历同知徽政院事，遂拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: He again passed through Associate Administrator of the Huizheng Commission, then was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He then served as associate administrator of the Huizheng Commission and was appointed vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 帝以其有疾，诏特免朝礼，光禄日给上尊。

translations.literal: Because he was ill, the emperor issued an edict specially exempting him from court ceremony; the Imperial Household Commission daily supplied him superior wine.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was ill, the emperor excused him from court attendance and ordered the Imperial Household Commission to supply him fine wine every day.

sentences.zh: 祖常持宪务存大体。

translations.literal: Zuchang upheld the law and strove to preserve the larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: As censor Zuchang upheld the law while keeping sight of larger principles.

sentences.zh: 西台御史劾其僚禁酤时面有酒容，以苛细黜之。

translations.literal: A censor of the Western Secretariat impeached a colleague who, during the prohibition on wine, had the look of drink on his face; Zuchang dismissed the accuser for petty severity.
translations.idiomatic: When a western secretariat censor impeached a colleague for looking drunk during a wine ban, Zuchang dismissed the accuser for excessive severity.

sentences.zh: 山东廉访司言孔氏讼事，以事关名教不行，按者亦引去。

translations.literal: The Shandong surveillance commission reported a lawsuit involving the Kong clan; because it touched fundamental teaching he did not proceed, and the investigator also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shandong surveillance commission reported a lawsuit involving the Kong clan, he declined to act because the case touched fundamental ritual teaching, and the investigating official withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 除枢密副使，顷之，辞职归光州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council; shortly thereafter he resigned and returned to Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice commissioner of the Privy Council, but soon resigned and returned to Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 复除江南行台中丞，又迁陕西行台中丞，皆以疾不赴。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Regional Secretariat and then transferred to Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Regional Secretariat; in each case he did not take up the post because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named censor-in-chief of Jiangnan and then of Shaanxi, but declined both appointments because of illness.

sentences.zh: 至元四年卒，年六十，赠摅忠宣宪协正功臣、河南行省右丞、上护军、魏郡公，谥文贞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhizheng he died at age sixty; posthumously enfeoffed as Meritorious Minister Who Displays Loyalty, Proclaims Integrity, and Harmonizes Rectitude, Right Councillor of the Henan Regional Secretariat, Senior Guardian General, and Duke of Wei Commandery; posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Zhizheng at the age of sixty. He was posthumously enfeoffed as meritorious minister, right councillor of the Henan regional secretariat, senior guardian general, and Duke of Wei, with the posthumous title Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 祖常立朝既久，多所建明。

translations.literal: Zuchang had long stood at court and proposed many enlightened measures.
translations.idiomatic: Having served at court for many years, Zuchang proposed numerous reforms.

sentences.zh: 尝议：今国族及诸部既诵圣贤之书，当知尊诸母以厚彝伦。

translations.literal: He once proposed: "Now that the imperial clan and the various tribes recite the books of the sages, they ought to know how to honor all mothers in order to thicken fundamental human relations."
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that since the imperial clan and the various tribes now studied the classics, they should honor all mothers properly to strengthen family ethics.

sentences.zh: 又议：将家子弟骄脆，有孤任使，而庶民有挽强蹶张老死草野者，当建武学、武举，储材以备非常。

translations.literal: He also proposed: "Sons and younger brothers of military families are arrogant and frail, yet some are left alone to bear appointments, while among common people there are those who can draw the strong bow and shoot the stiff bow yet die old in the wild grass—military schools and military examinations ought to be established to store talent against the unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that while sons of military families grew spoiled and weak, commoners skilled with the bow died forgotten in the fields; military schools and examinations should be created to train reserves for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 时虽弗用，识者韪之。

translations.literal: Although at the time they were not adopted, those with insight approved them.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not adopt these proposals at the time, but thoughtful men approved them.

sentences.zh: 祖常工于文章，宏赡而精核，务去陈言，专以先秦两汉为法，而自成一家之言。

translations.literal: Zuchang was skilled in literary composition—broad and rich yet precise and exacting; he strove to remove stale language and took the pre-Qin and the two Han as his models, yet formed a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Zuchang excelled at prose—expansive yet exacting, determined to shed stale phrasing, taking pre-Qin and Han writers as his models while developing a style distinctly his own.

sentences.zh: 尤致力于诗，圆密清丽，大篇短章无不可传者。

translations.literal: He devoted himself especially to poetry—rounded, dense, clear, and refined; whether long compositions or short pieces, none were unfit to be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted special effort to poetry, writing in a rounded, polished, and lucid style; long poems and short lyrics alike were fit to endure.

sentences.zh: 有文集行于世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 尝预修《英宗实录》，又译润《皇图大训》、《承华事略》，又编集《列后金鉴》、《千秋记略》以进，受赐优渥。

translations.literal: He once took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong, also translated and polished the Great Instruction of the Imperial Design and the Brief Account of the Flourishing Palace, also compiled and presented the Golden Mirror of Successive Empresses and the Brief Record of a Thousand Autumns, and received generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong, translated and polished the Great Instruction of the Imperial Design and the Brief Account of the Flourishing Palace, and compiled the Golden Mirror of Empresses and the Brief Record of a Thousand Autumns for presentation to the throne, receiving generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 文宗尝驻跸龙虎台，祖常应制赋诗，尤被叹赏，谓中原硕儒唯祖常云。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong once halted at Longhu Terrace; Zuchang composed a poem on imperial command and was especially admired; it was said that among the great scholars of the Central Plains only Zuchang could be named.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong halted at Longhu Terrace, Zuchang composed an imperial-command poem that won especial praise; courtiers said that among the great scholars of the Central Plains only Zuchang deserved the name.

sentences.zh: 巙巙字子山，康里氏。

translations.literal: Kuikui, style name Zishan, of the Kangli clan.
translations.idiomatic: Kuikui, whose style name was Zishan, was of the Kangli clan.

sentences.zh: 父不忽木，自有传。

translations.literal: His father Bayan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bayan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 祖燕真，事世祖，从征有功。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yanzhen served the Founder and followed the campaigns with merit.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yanzhen served Kublai and distinguished himself on campaign.

sentences.zh: 巙巙幼肄业国学，博通群书，其正心修身之要得诸许衡及父兄家传。

translations.literal: Kuikui in youth pursued his studies at the National University, broadly mastered the classics, and obtained the essentials of rectifying the mind and cultivating the person from Xu Heng and the family teachings of father and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Kuikui studied at the National University as a youth, mastered the classics broadly, and learned the essentials of moral self-cultivation from Xu Heng and from his father and elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 长袭宿卫，风神凝远，制行峻洁，望而知其为贵介公子。

translations.literal: When grown he inherited palace guard service; his bearing was remote and refined, his conduct stern and pure—one could tell at a glance that he was a noble young lord.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he inherited palace guard duty. His bearing was distant and refined, his conduct strict and pure; anyone could see at once that he was a nobleman's son.

sentences.zh: 其遇事英发，掀髯论辨，法家拂士不能过之。

translations.literal: When matters arose he was spirited and quick; stroking his beard in debate, Legalist debaters and persuaders could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: In debate he was quick and forceful, stroking his beard as he argued; legalist debaters and persuaders could not match him.

sentences.zh: 始授承直郎、集贤待制，迁兵部郎中，转秘书监丞。

translations.literal: He was first appointed Gentleman for Upholding Integrity and Academician-in-Waiting of the Jixian Hall, transferred to Director of the Ministry of War, then promoted to Vice-Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed gentleman for upholding integrity and Jixian academician-in-waiting, then director in the Ministry of War, and then vice-director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 奉命往核泉舶，芥视珠犀，不少留目。

translations.literal: Ordered to go audit Quanzhou shipping, he regarded pearls and rhinoceros horn as mustard seeds and did not linger his gaze on them.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to audit Quanzhou shipping, he treated pearls and rhinoceros horn as worthless and never gave them a second glance.

sentences.zh: 改同佥太常礼仪院事，拜监察御史，升河东廉访副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Associate Administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, appointed Investigating Censor, and promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Hedong Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He became associate administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made investigating censor, and was promoted to vice commissioner of the Hedong surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 未上，迁秘书太监，升侍仪使。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was transferred to Vice-Director of the Palace Library and promoted to Commissioner of Ceremonial Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the surveillance post he was made vice-director of the Palace Library and then commissioner of ceremonial attendance.

sentences.zh: 寻擢中书右司郎中，迁集贤直学士，转江南行台治书侍御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Director of the Right Section of the Central Secretariat, transferred to Hanlin Academician Expositor of the Jixian Hall, and moved to Associate Censor of the Secretariat on the Jiangnan Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to director of the Secretariat's right section, then Hanlin expositor of the Jixian Hall, and then associate censor on the Jiangnan regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 拜礼部尚书，监群玉内司。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Rites and supervised the Inner Office of the Jade Cluster.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Rites and supervised the Inner Office of the Jade Cluster.

sentences.zh: 巙巙正色率下。

translations.literal: Kuikui with stern countenance led his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Kuikui led his subordinates with stern dignity.

sentences.zh: 国制，大乐诸坊咸隶本部，遇公燕，众伎毕陈。

translations.literal: By national regulation, all the music workshops of the Great Music Bureau were subordinate to this ministry; when there was a public banquet, all performers were fully displayed.
translations.idiomatic: By court regulation all music troupes of the Great Music Bureau fell under his ministry; at state banquets every performer was put on display.

sentences.zh: 巙巙视之泊如，僚佐以下皆肃然。

translations.literal: Kuikui viewed them with utter calm; assistants and those below all became solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Kuikui watched them with complete detachment, and his staff grew solemn in his presence.

sentences.zh: 迁领会同馆事尚书，监群玉内司如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to lead the affairs of the Hall of Joint Assembly as Minister, while supervising the Inner Office of the Jade Cluster as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to head the Hall of Joint Assembly as minister while continuing to supervise the Inner Office of the Jade Cluster.

sentences.zh: 寻兼经筵官，复除江南行台治书侍御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently an officer of the Classics Lecture, and again appointed Associate Censor of the Secretariat on the Jiangnan Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also served on the classics lecture staff and was again appointed associate censor on the Jiangnan regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未行，留为奎章阁学士院承制学士，仍兼经筵官。

translations.literal: Before he departed he was retained as Academician Drafter of the Kui Zhang Pavilion Academy, still concurrently an officer of the Classics Lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave he was kept at court as drafting academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion Academy while retaining his classics lecture post.

sentences.zh: 升侍书学士、同知经筵事，复升奎章阁学士院大学士、知经筵事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician Attendant for Writing and Associate Director of Classics Lecture Affairs, then again promoted to Grand Academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion Academy and Director of Classics Lecture Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant-writing academician and associate director of classics lecture affairs, then to grand academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion Academy and director of those affairs.

sentences.zh: 除浙西廉访使，复留为大学士、知经筵事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Western Zhe, but again retained as Grand Academician and Director of Classics Lecture Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed surveillance commissioner of Western Zhe but was again kept at court as grand academician and director of classics lecture affairs.

sentences.zh: 寻拜翰林学士承旨、知制诰兼修国史、知经筵事，提调宣文阁崇文监。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, Drafter of Imperial Proclamations with concurrent duty revising the National History and directing Classics Lecture Affairs, and supervised the Xuanwen Pavilion and Chongwen Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Hanlin academician recipient of edicts, drafter of imperial proclamations, reviser of the national history, and director of classics lecture affairs, with overall charge of the Xuanwen Pavilion and Chongwen Directorate.

sentences.zh: 先是，文宗励精图治，巙巙尝以圣贤格言讲诵帝侧，裨益良多。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wenzong strove to govern diligently, Kuikui had often expounded the maxims of the sages and worthies at the emperor's side, with much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Wenzong strove to govern well, Kuikui had often expounded the sages' maxims at his side to great effect.

sentences.zh: 顺帝即位之后，剪除权奸，思更治化。

translations.literal: After Emperor Shundi ascended the throne, he cut down powerful traitors and thought to renew the transformation of government.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shundi came to the throne he eliminated powerful traitors and sought to renew good government.

sentences.zh: 巙巙侍经筵，日劝帝务学，帝辄就之习授，欲宠以师礼，巙巙力辞不可。

translations.literal: Kuikui attended the classics lecture, daily urging the emperor to devote himself to learning; the emperor would go to him for instruction and wished to honor him with the rites due a teacher, but Kuikui strenuously declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Serving on the classics lecture staff, Kuikui daily urged the emperor to study; the emperor came to him for instruction and wished to honor him with a teacher's rites, but Kuikui firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 凡《四书》、《六经》所载治道，为帝绎而言，必使辞达感动帝衷敷暢旨意而后已。

translations.literal: Whatever governing principles were recorded in the Four Books and Six Classics, he expounded for the emperor, always making the words reach through, move the emperor's heart, and spread his intent fully before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever principles of governance appeared in the Four Books and Six Classics, he expounded for the emperor until his words reached the throne, moved the emperor's heart, and carried his meaning fully home.

sentences.zh: 若柳宗元《梓人传》、张商英《七臣论》，尤喜诵说。

translations.literal: Such works as Liu Zongyuan's Biography of the Master Carpenter and Zhang Shangying's Treatise on the Seven Ministers he especially delighted to recite and explain.
translations.idiomatic: He especially liked to recite and explain such texts as Liu Zongyuan's Biography of the Master Carpenter and Zhang Shangying's Treatise on the Seven Ministers.

sentences.zh: 尝于经筵力陈商英所言七臣之状，左右错愕，有嫉之之色，然素知其贤，不复肆愠。

translations.literal: Once at the classics lecture he forcefully set forth the forms of the seven ministers described by Shangying; those at left and right were startled and showed jealousy, yet knowing his worth from of old they did not again vent anger freely.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the lecture he forcefully described Zhang Shangying's seven types of ministers; those around the throne were startled and jealous, but knowing his worth they did not vent their anger.

sentences.zh: 帝暇日欲观古名画，巙巙即取郭忠恕《比干图》以进，因言商王受不听忠臣之谏，遂亡其国。

translations.literal: On a day of leisure the emperor wished to view famous ancient paintings; Kuikui immediately took Guo Zhongshu's Picture of Bigan to present, and thereby said that King Shou of Shang did not heed loyal ministers' remonstrances and thereby lost his state.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to view famous paintings on a day of leisure, Kuikui presented Guo Zhongshu's Picture of Bigan and explained that King Zhou of Shang ignored loyal remonstrance and lost his realm.

sentences.zh: 帝一日览宋徽宗画称善，巙巙进言，徽宗多能，惟一事不能。

translations.literal: One day the emperor viewed paintings of Emperor Huizong of Song and praised them; Kuikui advanced a remark: "Huizong had many abilities, but one thing he could not do."
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor praised a painting by Emperor Huizong of Song; Kuikui said, "Huizong had many talents, but one thing he could not do."

sentences.zh: 帝问何谓一事。

translations.literal: The emperor asked what the one thing was.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what that one thing was.

sentences.zh: 对曰：「独不能为君尔。

translations.literal: He replied: "He alone could not be a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "He alone could not be a ruler.

sentences.zh: 身辱国破，皆由不能为君所致。

translations.literal: Personal disgrace and the state's destruction all came from his inability to be a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: His personal ruin and the fall of the state all stemmed from his failure as a ruler.

sentences.zh: 人君贵能为君，它非所尚也。」

translations.literal: For a ruler it is precious to be able to be a ruler; other things are not what should be prized."
translations.idiomatic: What matters for a ruler is to rule well; other accomplishments are not what should be prized."

sentences.zh: 或遇天变民灾，必忧见于色，乘间则进言于帝曰：「天心仁，爱人君，故以变示儆。

translations.literal: Whenever there were celestial anomalies or disasters among the people, worry always showed on his face; seizing an opportunity he would advance words to the emperor, saying: "Heaven's heart is benevolent and loves the ruler; therefore it displays anomalies as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever heaven sent omens or the people suffered disaster, worry showed on his face, and he would seize the chance to tell the emperor, "Heaven is benevolent and loves its ruler; that is why it sends warnings through anomalies.

sentences.zh: 譬如慈父于子，爱则教之戒之。

translations.literal: It is like a loving father toward his son—because he loves him he teaches and admonishes him.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a loving father toward his son: because he loves the child, he teaches and warns him.

sentences.zh: 子能起敬起孝，则父怒必释。

translations.literal: If the son can rouse respect and rouse filial piety, then the father's anger must be released.
translations.idiomatic: If the son becomes respectful and filial, the father's anger will surely pass.

sentences.zh: 人君侧身修行，则天意必回。」

translations.literal: If the ruler corrects his person and cultivates virtue, then Heaven's intent must turn back."
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler reforms himself and cultivates virtue, Heaven's intent will surely turn favorable again."

sentences.zh: 帝察其真诚，虚己以听。

translations.literal: The emperor perceived his sincerity and emptied himself to listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw his sincerity and listened with an open mind.

sentences.zh: 特赐只孙燕服九袭及玉带楮币，以旌其言。

translations.literal: He was specially granted nine sets of zhisun banquet robes and a jade belt with paper money, to honor his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially granted him nine sets of zhisun banquet robes, a jade belt, and paper money to honor his counsel.

sentences.zh: 巙巙尝谓人曰：「天下事在宰相当言，宰相不得言则台谏言之，台谏不敢言则经筵言之。

translations.literal: Kuikui once said to others: "Affairs under Heaven ought to be spoken of by the chief councillor; if the chief councillor may not speak, then the censorate speaks; if the censorate dares not speak, then the classics lecture speaks.
translations.idiomatic: Kuikui once said, "Affairs of state are for the chief councillor to speak about; if he will not, the censorate should; if the censorate will not, the classics lecture should.

sentences.zh: 备位经筵，得言人所不敢言于天子之前，志愿足矣。」

translations.literal: Occupying a post on the classics lecture, to be able to speak what others dare not speak before the Son of Heaven—my wish is already fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: Holding a place on the classics lecture staff and being able to say before the Son of Heaven what others dare not say is ambition enough for me."

sentences.zh: 故于时政得失有当匡救者，未尝缄默。

translations.literal: Therefore regarding gains and losses in current government, whenever there was something that ought to be rectified and saved, he never kept silent.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore whenever current policy needed correction he never kept silent.

sentences.zh: 大臣议罢先朝所置奎章阁学士院及艺文监诸属官。

translations.literal: Great ministers discussed abolishing the Kui Zhang Pavilion Academy and the subordinate offices of the Directorate of Literary Arts established by the previous reign.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers proposed abolishing the Kui Zhang Pavilion Academy and the subordinate offices of the Directorate of Literary Arts established under the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 巙巙进曰：「民有千金之产，犹设家塾，延馆客，岂有堂堂天朝，富有四海，一学房乃不能容耶？」

translations.literal: Kuikui advanced and said: "When common people have property worth a thousand gold, they still set up a family school and invite resident tutors—how could there be a majestic heavenly court, rich in all within the four seas, yet unable to accommodate a single schoolroom?"
translations.idiomatic: Kuikui objected, "A family with a thousand pieces of gold still keeps a private school and hires tutors. How can a great dynasty that owns the four seas lack room for one school?"

sentences.zh: 帝闻而深然之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard him and strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 即日改奎章阁为宣文阁，艺文监为崇文监，存设如初，就命巙巙董治。

translations.literal: That very day the Kui Zhang Pavilion was changed to the Xuanwen Pavilion and the Directorate of Literary Arts to the Chongwen Directorate; establishments were preserved as at first, and Kuikui was immediately ordered to supervise and govern them.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Kui Zhang Pavilion was renamed the Xuanwen Pavilion and the Directorate of Literary Arts the Chongwen Directorate; the institutions were kept as before and Kuikui was put in charge.

sentences.zh: 又请置检讨等职十六员以备进讲。

translations.literal: He also requested establishing sixteen posts such as Reviser to prepare for advancing lectures.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that sixteen posts such as reviser be created to support the lecture program.

sentences.zh: 帝皆俞允。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these requests.

sentences.zh: 时科举既辍，巙巙从容为帝言：「古昔取人材以济世用，必由科举，何可废也。」

translations.literal: At that time the civil examinations had already been halted; Kuikui calmly said to the emperor: "In antiquity and the past, obtaining human talent to aid worldly employment always had to go through the examinations—how could they be abolished?"
translations.idiomatic: Civil examinations had been suspended; Kuikui calmly told the emperor, "From antiquity onward talent for public service has always been recruited through examinations. How can they be abandoned?"

sentences.zh: 帝采其论，寻复旧制。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted his argument; before long the old system was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his view and soon restored the old examination system.

sentences.zh: 一日，进读司马光《资治通鉴》，因言国家当及斯时修辽、金、宋三史，岁久恐致阙逸。

translations.literal: One day, advancing in lecture Sima Guang's Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, he thereby said the state ought at this time compile the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; as years pass, fear arises of omissions and loss.
translations.idiomatic: One day, lecturing on Sima Guang's Comprehensive Mirror, he said the dynasty ought now to compile the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song before long delay caused records to be lost.

sentences.zh: 后置纂修，实由巙巙发其端。

translations.literal: The later establishment of compilation and revision in fact began from Kuikui's initiative.
translations.idiomatic: The later project to compile those histories in fact began with Kuikui's suggestion.

sentences.zh: 又请行乡饮酒于国学，使民知逊悌，及请褒赠唐刘蕡、宋邵雍以旌道德正直。

translations.literal: He also requested carrying out the village drinking ceremony at the National University so the people would know modesty and brotherly deference, and requested posthumous enfeoffment and gifts for Liu Zan of Tang and Shao Yong of Song to honor moral uprightness and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the village drinking ceremony be held at the National University to teach the people modesty and deference, and that posthumous honors be granted to Liu Zan of Tang and Shao Yong of Song to commend moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 帝从其请，为之下诏。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his request and issued an edict for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his requests and issued edicts accordingly.

sentences.zh: 巙巙以重望居高位，而雅爱儒士，甚于饥渴，以故四方士大夫翕然宗之，萃于其门。

translations.literal: Kuikui, by heavy reputation occupying a high position, yet elegantly loved Confucian scholars more than hunger and thirst; for this reason scholars and officials from the four directions with one accord took him as their patron and gathered at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Kuikui held high office with great prestige and loved scholars with an eagerness surpassing hunger and thirst, so men of letters from every quarter flocked to him as their patron.

sentences.zh: 达官有怙势者，言曰：「儒有何好，君酷爱之。」

translations.literal: A high official who relied on power said: "What is good about Confucians that you love them so ardently?"
translations.idiomatic: A powerful official said to him, "What is so fine about Confucians that you adore them so?"

sentences.zh: 巙巙曰：「世祖以儒足以致治，命裕宗学于赞善王恂。

translations.literal: Kuikui said: "The Founder held that Confucian learning was sufficient to bring about good government and ordered Prince Yu study under the Tutor Wang Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Kuikui replied, "Kublai believed Confucian learning could bring good government and had Prince Yu study under the tutor Wang Xun.

sentences.zh: 今秘书所藏裕宗仿书，当时御笔于学生之下亲署御名习书谨呈，其敬慎若此。

translations.literal: Now the copybook preserved in the Secretariat by Prince Yu—in those days the imperial brush personally signed the imperial name beneath the student's name, "Diligently presented for study of writing"—was so reverent and careful as this.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat still keeps Prince Yu's copybook practice sheets, on which the emperor personally signed his name beneath the prince's with the note "Diligently presented for writing practice"—such was the reverence shown.

sentences.zh: 世祖尝暮召我先人坐寝榻下，陈说《四书》及古史治乱，至丙夜不寐。

translations.literal: The Founder once at dusk summoned my forebear to sit below the sleeping couch, expounding the Four Books and the rise and fall in ancient histories, until the third watch without sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai once summoned my grandfather at dusk to sit by his couch and expound the Four Books and the rise and fall of states in history, talking until the third watch without sleeping.

sentences.zh: 世祖喜曰：『朕所以令卿从许仲平学，正欲卿以嘉言入告朕耳，卿益加懋敬以副朕志。』

translations.literal: The Founder rejoiced and said: "The reason I ordered you to study with Xu Zhongping is precisely that I wished you to enter good words to inform me; you should further increase your earnest reverence to fulfill my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said with pleasure, "I had you study with Xu Heng so you could bring good counsel to me. Be still more earnest in fulfilling my wish."

sentences.zh: 今汝言不爱儒，宁不念圣祖神宗笃好之意乎？

translations.literal: Now you say you do not love Confucians—do you not recall the profound devotion of the sacred ancestor and divine founder?
translations.idiomatic: Now you say you dislike Confucians—have you forgotten how deeply our sacred ancestors loved them?

sentences.zh: 且儒者之道，从之则君仁、臣忠、父慈、子孝，人伦咸得，国家咸治；

translations.literal: Moreover the Way of the Confucians—if followed, then the ruler is benevolent, ministers loyal, fathers kind, sons filial, human relations all obtained, the state all well governed;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, follow the Confucian Way and the ruler becomes benevolent, ministers loyal, fathers kind, and sons filial; human relations are secured and the state is well governed.

sentences.zh: 违之则人伦咸失，家国咸乱。

translations.literal: if violated, then human relations all lost, family and state all in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Violate it and human relations collapse and family and state fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 汝欲乱而家，吾弗能御，汝慎勿以斯言乱我国也。

translations.literal: If you wish to disorder your own house, I cannot restrain you; take care not to disorder our state with such words.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to ruin your own household I cannot stop you, but take care not to ruin our state with such talk.

sentences.zh: 儒者或身若不胜衣，言若不出口，然腹中贮储有过人者，何可易视也。」

translations.literal: Confucians may seem as if their bodies cannot bear clothes and as if words will not leave their mouths, yet what is stored in their bellies surpasses others—how can they be lightly regarded?"
translations.idiomatic: Some Confucians look frail and speak softly, yet their minds hold more than others. How can they be lightly dismissed?"

sentences.zh: 达官色惭。

translations.literal: The high official's face showed shame.
translations.idiomatic: The official blushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 既而出拜江浙行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Thereafter he went out and was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He then left the capital and was appointed pacification commissioner of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，复以翰林学士承旨召还。

translations.literal: The next year he was again summoned back as Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled as Hanlin academician recipient of edicts.

sentences.zh: 时中书平章阙员，近臣欲有所荐用，以言觇帝意。

translations.literal: At that time a vacancy existed for Pacification Commissioner of the Central Secretariat; close attendants wished to recommend someone for use and probed the emperor's intent with words.
translations.idiomatic: When a post as Secretariat pacification commissioner fell vacant, courtiers wished to recommend someone and sounded out the emperor's preference.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「平章已有其人，今行半途矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The pacification commissioner already has his man—he is now halfway on the journey."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The pacification commissioner has already been chosen—he is halfway back now."

sentences.zh: 近臣知帝意在巙巙，不复荐人。

translations.literal: The close attendants knew the emperor's intent lay with Kuikui and no longer recommended others.
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers understood that the emperor meant Kuikui and made no further recommendations.

sentences.zh: 至京七日，感热疾卒，实至正五年五月辛卯也，年五十一。

translations.literal: Seven days after reaching the capital he contracted a heat illness and died—it was in fact the xinmao day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Zhizheng, age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days after reaching the capital he died of heat illness on the xinmao day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Zhizheng, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 家贫，几无以为敛。

translations.literal: His family was poor; there was almost nothing with which to lay him out for burial.
translations.idiomatic: His family was so poor they could scarcely afford his funeral.

sentences.zh: 帝闻，为震悼，赐赙银五锭。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he was shaken with grief and granted five ingots of silver for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved and granted five ingots of silver for funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 其所负官中营运钱，台臣奏以罚布为之代偿。

translations.literal: The operating funds he owed to the government—censorate officials memorialized that cloth levied as fines should be used to repay them on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Censors memorialized that fines collected in cloth should repay the operating funds he still owed the government.

sentences.zh: 巙巙善真行草书，识者谓得晋人笔意，单牍片纸，人争宝之，不翅金玉。

translations.literal: Kuikui was skilled in regular, running, and cursive script; connoisseurs said he obtained the brush intent of Jin men; a single slip or fragment of paper—people competed to treasure it, no less than gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Kuikui excelled at regular, running, and cursive script; connoisseurs said he captured the spirit of Jin calligraphy, and people treasured even a single slip of his writing as dearly as gold or jade.

sentences.zh: 谥文忠。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 兄回回，字子渊。

translations.literal: His elder brother Huihui, style name Ziyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Huihui, whose style name was Ziyuan.

sentences.zh: 敦默寡言，耆学能文。

translations.literal: Steadfast and silent, sparing of words, aged in learning and able in letters.
translations.idiomatic: He was steady and reticent, deeply learned, and skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 在成宗朝宿卫，擢太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: During Emperor Chengzong's reign he served in palace guard and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chengzong he served in the palace guard and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 寺改为院，为太常院使。

translations.literal: When the temple office was changed to a commission, he became Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the office was reorganized as a commission he became its director.

sentences.zh: 武宗正位，以籓邸旧臣出使称旨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, as an old follower of the princely residence on embassy he pleased the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, Huihui, an old follower from his princely household, served on embassy and pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 至大间，调大司农卿，除山南廉访使，改江南行台治书侍御史，迁淮西廉访使，皆有政声。

translations.literal: During the Zhida era he was transferred to Director of the Grand Commission for Agriculture, appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Shannan, changed to Associate Censor of the Secretariat on the Jiangnan Regional Secretariat, transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Huaixi—all with reputations for good government.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhida era he served as director of the Grand Commission for Agriculture, surveillance commissioner of Shannan, associate censor on the Jiangnan regional secretariat, and surveillance commissioner of Huaixi, earning a reputation for good administration at each post.

sentences.zh: 再改河南廉访使。

translations.literal: He was again changed to Surveillance Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed surveillance commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 行省丞相行事多不法，太尉纳璘为郎中，每格不下，丞相怒欲出之。

translations.literal: The regional secretariat chief councillor's conduct was often unlawful; Grand Marshal Nalin as director repeatedly blocked documents from descending; the chief councillor in anger wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan regional chief councillor often acted unlawfully; Nalin, serving as a bureau director, repeatedly blocked his orders, and the councillor angrily tried to have him removed.

sentences.zh: 回回察其贤，抗章举任风宪，后历三台，为名臣。

translations.literal: Huihui perceived his worth and submitted a forceful memorial recommending him for surveillance duties; later he passed through the three censorates and became a famous minister.
translations.idiomatic: Huihui recognized Nalin's talent and memorialized to appoint him to surveillance work; Nalin later served in all three censorates and became a famous minister.

sentences.zh: 驸马平章家奴强市人物，按之无所贷。

translations.literal: A chief councillor who was an imperial son-in-law's household slaves forcibly bought goods in the market; investigating them he showed no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: When the household slaves of an imperial son-in-law who was chief councillor forcibly bought goods in the market, he investigated them without mercy.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，丞相拜住首荐为户部尚书，寻拜南台侍御史，改参议中书。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Chief Councillor Bayan first recommended him as Minister of Revenue; soon he was appointed Attendant Censor of the Southern Secretariat and changed to Participant in Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong came to the throne, Chief Councillor Bayan first recommended him as Minister of Revenue; he was soon made attendant censor of the Southern Secretariat and then participant in Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 以议定刑书如法，帝嘉纳其奏。

translations.literal: Because he deliberated on fixing the penal code according to law, the emperor praised and adopted his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and adopted his memorial on revising the penal code in accordance with law.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，廷议漕运事，奏减粮数以纾东南民力。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding, in court deliberation on grain transport affairs, he memorialized to reduce grain quotas to ease the strength of the people in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiding reign, when the court debated grain transport, he memorialized to reduce quotas and ease the burden on the people of the southeast.

sentences.zh: 授太子詹事丞，改山东廉访使，未上，升翰林侍讲学士，迁江浙行省右丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice-Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent, changed to Surveillance Commissioner of Shandong; before taking up the post he was promoted to Hanlin Academician Explaining the Classics and transferred to Right Councillor of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice-director of the heir apparent's household, then surveillance commissioner of Shandong; before taking up that post he was promoted to Hanlin lecturing academician and made right councillor of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，除宣政院使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong was established, he was appointed Director of the Xuanzheng Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong came to the throne, he was appointed director of the Xuanzheng Commission.

sentences.zh: 上言乞沙汰僧道，其所有田宜同民间征输。

translations.literal: He submitted words requesting screening and reduction of monks and Daoists; the fields they possessed ought to be taxed and supplied like those of common people.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to reduce the number of monks and Daoists and to tax their landholdings like ordinary fields.

sentences.zh: 擢中书右丞，力辞还第。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Councillor of the Central Secretariat and strenuously declined, returning to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right councillor of the Central Secretariat but firmly declined and returned home.

sentences.zh: 闻明宗崩，流涕不能食，自是杜门不出者数年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: Hearing that Emperor Mingzong had died, he wept and could not eat; from then he shut his gate and did not go out for several years, and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Emperor Mingzong had died, he wept and could not eat; he shut his doors and did not go out for years, and eventually died of illness.

sentences.zh: 与弟巙巙皆为时之名臣，世号为双璧云。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Kuikui were both famous ministers of the time; the age called them a pair of jade disks.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Kuikui were both celebrated ministers of their day, and contemporaries called them a pair of jade disks.

sentences.zh: 巙巙子维山，材质清劭，侍禁廷，起崇文监丞，擢给事中，迁同佥太常礼仪院事，调崇文太监。

translations.literal: Kuikui's son Weishan, of clear and vigorous character, attended at the forbidden court; he began as Vice-Director of the Chongwen Directorate, was promoted to Supervising Censor, transferred to Associate Administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was moved to Vice-Director of the Chongwen Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Kuikui's son Weishan was refined and vigorous in character, served at court, rose from vice-director of the Chongwen Directorate to supervising censor, then associate administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and finally vice-director of the Chongwen Directorate.

sentences.zh: 自当，蒙古人也。

translations.literal: Zidang was a Mongol.
translations.idiomatic: Zidang was a Mongol.

sentences.zh: 英宗时，由速古兒赤擢监察御史。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yingzong's reign, from night guard he was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yingzong he was promoted from night guard to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 录囚大兴县，有以冤事系狱者，其人尝见有橐驼死道傍，因舁至其家醢之，置数甕中。

translations.literal: Recording prisoners in Daxing County, there was one imprisoned on a wrongful matter: the man had once seen a Bactrian camel dead by the roadside and therefore carried it to his home to pickle it, placing it in several jars.
translations.idiomatic: While reviewing prisoners in Daxing County he found a man wrongly imprisoned: the man had once seen a Bactrian camel dead by the road, carried it home to pickle, and stored the meat in several jars.

sentences.zh: 会官橐驼被盗，捕索甚亟，乃执而勘之，其人自诬服。

translations.literal: It happened that government Bactrian camels were stolen; arrest and search were very urgent; they therefore seized and examined him, and the man falsely confessed guilt himself.
translations.idiomatic: When government camels were stolen and the search was urgent, officials seized and interrogated him, and he falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 自当审其狱辞，疑为冤，即以上御史臺。

translations.literal: Zidang examined his prison testimony, suspected a wrongful case, and immediately reported upward to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Zidang examined the case, suspected a miscarriage of justice, and reported it to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 台臣以为赃既具，是特御史畏杀人耳，不听，改委他御史谳之，竟处死。

translations.literal: Censorate officials thought the stolen goods were already complete—it was merely that the censor feared killing—and would not listen; they changed and entrusted another censor to judge the case, and in the end he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate officials thought the evidence of theft was complete and that Zidang merely feared executing a man; they refused to listen, assigned another censor to judge the case, and the man was executed.

sentences.zh: 后数日，辽阳行省以获盗闻，冤始白，人以是服其明。

translations.literal: Several days later the Liaoyang Regional Secretariat reported capturing the thieves; the wrongful case was first cleared, and people for this reason submitted to his perspicacity.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the Liaoyang regional secretariat reported the real thieves captured, and the man's innocence was proved; people admired Zidang's discernment.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，扈从至上都，纠言参知政事杨庭玉赃罪，不报，即纳印还京师。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiding, escorting the emperor to Shangdu, he impeached Associate Administrator Yang Tingyu for corrupt crimes; when no reply came, he immediately returned his seal and went back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiding, while escorting the emperor to Shangdu, he impeached Associate Administrator Yang Tingyu for corruption; when no response came, he surrendered his seal and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使追之，俾复任。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to pursue him and ordered him to resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys after him and ordered him to resume office.

sentences.zh: 即再上章劾庭玉，竟如其言。

translations.literal: He immediately submitted another memorial impeaching Tingyu, and in the end it was as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately impeached Tingyu again, and events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 以劾奏平章政事秃满迭兒入怯薛之日，英宗被弑，必预闻其谋，不省，乃赐秃满迭兒黄金系腰，自当遂辞职。

translations.literal: Because he had impeached Pacification Commissioner Tumanadier on the day he entered the kheshig, and Emperor Yingzong was assassinated—he must have foreknown the plot—yet was not investigated; instead Tumanadier was granted a gold waist belt; Zidang thereupon resigned.
translations.idiomatic: He had impeached Pacification Commissioner Tumanadier on the very day Tumanadier entered the imperial guard, and Emperor Yingzong was assassinated soon after—Zidang must have foreseen the plot. Yet no inquiry followed; instead Tumanadier was rewarded with a gold waist belt, and Zidang resigned.

sentences.zh: 改工部员外郎，中书省委开混河，自当往视之，以为水性不常，民力亦瘁，难以成功，言于朝，河役乃罢。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works; the Central Secretariat commissioned opening the Hun River; Zidang went to inspect it, thought the water's nature was not constant and the people's strength also exhausted, that success would be hard, spoke to the court, and the river labor was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Ministry of Works. When the Secretariat ordered the Hun River opened, Zidang inspected the project, judged the watercourse unstable and the people exhausted, told the court success was unlikely, and the river works were halted.

sentences.zh: 会次三皇后殂，命工部撤行殿车帐，皆新作之。

translations.literal: It happened that the third consort queen died; the Ministry of Works was ordered to remove the traveling palace carts and tents and make all new ones.
translations.idiomatic: When the third consort queen died, the Ministry of Works was ordered to discard the traveling palace carts and tents and make new ones.

sentences.zh: 自当未即兴工。

translations.literal: Zidang had not yet immediately begun the work.
translations.idiomatic: Zidang had not yet begun the work.

sentences.zh: 尚书曰：「此奉特旨，员外有误，则罪归于众矣。」

translations.literal: The minister said: "This follows a special edict; if the vice director errs, guilt will fall on the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: The minister said, "This follows a special edict. If you err, the whole office will be blamed."

sentences.zh: 自当曰：「即有罪，我独任之。」

translations.literal: Zidang said: "If there is guilt, I alone bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Zidang said, "If there is blame, I alone will bear it."

sentences.zh: 未几，帝果问成否。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor indeed asked whether it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor indeed asked whether the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 省臣乃召自当责问之。

translations.literal: Secretariat officials thereupon summoned Zidang and reproached him with questions.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat officials summoned Zidang to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 自当请自入对。

translations.literal: Zidang requested to enter and answer in person.
translations.idiomatic: Zidang asked to answer the emperor in person.

sentences.zh: 既见帝，奏曰：「皇后行殿车帐尚新，若改作之，恐劳民费财。

translations.literal: Having seen the emperor, he memorialized: "The queen's traveling palace carts and tents are still new; if they are remade, I fear laboring the people and wasting wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw the emperor he said, "The queen's traveling carts and tents are still new. Remaking them would waste the people's labor and the state's wealth.

sentences.zh: 且先皇后无恶疾，居之何嫌。

translations.literal: Moreover the former queen had no malignant illness—what taboo is there in dwelling in them?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the late queen died of no contagious illness—what objection is there to using them?

sentences.zh: 必欲舍旧更新，则大明殿乃自世祖所御，列圣嗣位岂皆改作乎？」

translations.literal: If one must abandon the old and renew, then the Great Bright Hall was from the Founder himself used—did successive sacred emperors on succeeding to the throne all remake it?"
translations.idiomatic: If old things must always be replaced, should the Great Bright Hall, which Kublai himself used, be rebuilt every time an emperor succeeded to the throne?"

sentences.zh: 帝大悦，语省臣曰；

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said to Secretariat officials:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and told the Secretariat officials,

sentences.zh: 「国家用人，当择如自当者，庶不误大事。」

translations.literal: "In employing men for the state, one ought to choose such as Zidang, so that great affairs may not be mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: "In appointing officials the state should choose men like Zidang, so that great affairs are not mishandled."

sentences.zh: 特赐上尊、金币，迁吏部员外郎。

translations.literal: He was specially granted superior wine and gold coins and transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially rewarded with fine wine and gold and promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝欲加号太后曰太皇太后，命朝堂议之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to add the title Grand Empress Dowager to the empress dowager and ordered the court to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to give the empress dowager the title Grand Empress Dowager and ordered the court to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 自当独曰：「太后称太皇太后，于典礼不合。」

translations.literal: Zidang alone said: "For the empress dowager to be styled Grand Empress Dowager does not accord with ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: Zidang alone objected, "The title Grand Empress Dowager does not accord with ritual propriety for this empress dowager."

sentences.zh: 众皆曰：「英宗何以加皇太后号曰太皇太后？」

translations.literal: All said: "How did Emperor Yingzong add to the empress dowager the title Grand Empress Dowager?"
translations.idiomatic: Everyone asked, "Why did Emperor Yingzong give his empress dowager the title Grand Empress Dowager?"

sentences.zh: 自当曰：「英宗孙也，今上子也，太皇太后之号孙可以称之，子不可以称之也。」

translations.literal: Zidang said: "Emperor Yingzong was a grandson; the present emperor is a son. The title Grand Empress Dowager a grandson may apply, a son may not apply."
translations.idiomatic: Zidang answered, "Emperor Yingzong was a grandson of the empress dowager; the present emperor is her son. A grandson may use the title Grand Empress Dowager, but a son may not."

sentences.zh: 议遂定。

translations.literal: The deliberation was thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The debate was settled on that basis.

sentences.zh: 迁中书客省使，俄改同佥宣政院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Envoy of the Secretariat Guest Office, soon changed to Associate Administrator of the Xuanzheng Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to envoy of the Secretariat guest office and soon made associate administrator of the Xuanzheng Commission.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，除中书左司郎中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he was appointed Director of the Left Section of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong came to the throne, he was appointed director of the Secretariat's left section.

sentences.zh: 有使持诏自江浙还，言行省臣意若有不服者。

translations.literal: An envoy bearing an edict returned from Jiangsu-Zhejiang and said the regional secretariat ministers' intent seemed somewhat disobedient.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy returning from Jiangsu-Zhejiang with an edict reported that the regional officials seemed discontented.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命遣使问不敬状，将悉诛之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered envoys sent to inquire into the form of disrespect; he would execute them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered envoys sent to investigate their disrespect, intending to execute them all.

sentences.zh: 自当言于丞相燕帖木兒曰：「皇帝新即位，雲南、四川且犹未定，乃以使臣一言杀行省大臣，恐非盛德事。

translations.literal: Zidang spoke to Chief Councillor El Temür: "The emperor has newly ascended the throne; Yunnan and Sichuan are still not settled—yet on one envoy's word to kill regional secretariat great ministers, I fear this is not an affair of abundant virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zidang told Chief Councillor El Temür, "The emperor has only just ascended the throne, and Yunnan and Sichuan are still unsettled. To execute regional ministers on one envoy's word would hardly be an act of great virtue.

sentences.zh: 况江浙豪奢之地，使臣或不得厌其所需，则造言以陷之耳。」

translations.literal: Moreover Jiangsu-Zhejiang is a region of luxury and extravagance; if envoys perhaps do not obtain satisfaction of their needs, they then fabricate words to entrap others."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Jiangsu-Zhejiang is a wealthy region; if an envoy's demands are not met, he may invent charges to ruin officials."

sentences.zh: 燕帖木兒以言于帝，事乃止。

translations.literal: El Temür spoke thus to the emperor, and the affair was halted.
translations.idiomatic: El Temür relayed this to the emperor, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 既而升参议中书省事。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was promoted to Participant in the Affairs of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to participant in Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 燕帖木兒议封太保伯颜王爵，众论附之。

translations.literal: El Temür deliberated on enfeoffing Grand Guardian Bayan with a princely rank; the multitude's discussion attached to it.
translations.idiomatic: El Temür proposed ennobling Grand Guardian Bayan as a prince, and most officials agreed.

sentences.zh: 自当独不言。

translations.literal: Zidang alone did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Zidang alone remained silent.

sentences.zh: 燕帖木兒问故，自当曰：「太保位列三公，而复加王封，后再有大功，将何以处之？

translations.literal: El Temür asked the reason; Zidang said: "The Grand Guardian's rank stands among the Three Dukes, yet again to add princely enfeoffment—if later there is again great merit, how will he be treated?
translations.idiomatic: When El Temür asked why, Zidang said, "The Grand Guardian already ranks among the Three Dukes. If you add a princely title now, what reward remains if he renders still greater service later?

sentences.zh: 且丞相封王，出自上意，今欲加太保王封，丞相宜请于上。

translations.literal: Moreover when the chief councillor was enfeoffed as prince, it came from the upper intent; now wishing to add princely enfeoffment to the Grand Guardian, the chief councillor ought to request it from above.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover when the chief councillor received a princely title it came from the emperor's own wish. If you wish to ennoble the Grand Guardian now, you should ask the emperor directly.

sentences.zh: 王爵非中书选法也。」

translations.literal: Princely ranks are not within the Central Secretariat's selection law."
translations.idiomatic: Princely titles are not within the Secretariat's power to grant."

sentences.zh: 遂罢其议。

translations.literal: The deliberation was thereupon halted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 拜治书侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Associate Censor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed associate censor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，文宗在集庆潜邸，欲创天灵寺，令有司起民夫。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wenzong was at the hidden residence in Jiqing, he wished to create the Tianling Temple and ordered the authorities to raise corvée laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wenzong was prince at Jiqing, he wished to build the Tianling Temple and ordered officials to levy laborers.

sentences.zh: 江南行台监察御史亦乞剌台言曰：「太子为好事，宜出钱募夫，若欲役民，则朝廷闻之非便也。」

translations.literal: Jiangnan Regional Secretariat Investigating Censor Yeqilutai said: "The heir apparent is fond of undertaking affairs; he ought to disburse money to recruit laborers. If he wishes to conscript the people, then when the court hears of it, it will not be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan investigating censor Yeqilutai said, "The prince likes grand projects and should pay to hire workers. If he conscripts the people, the court will hear of it with displeasure."

sentences.zh: 至是文宗悉召江南行台监察御史，俾皆入为监察御史，而欲黜亦乞剌台。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Wenzong summoned all Jiangnan Regional Secretariat investigating censors, ordering them all to enter service as investigating censors, yet wished to dismiss Yeqilutai.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wenzong summoned all the Jiangnan investigating censors to the capital as investigating censors but wished to dismiss Yeqilutai.

sentences.zh: 自当谏曰：「当陛下在潜邸时，御史尽心为陛下言，乃忠臣也。

translations.literal: Zidang remonstrated: "When Your Majesty was at the hidden residence, the censor with full heart spoke for Your Majesty—he is a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zidang remonstrated, "When Your Majesty was still a prince, this censor spoke frankly for you. That is the conduct of a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 今无罪而黜之，非所以示天下。」

translations.literal: Now to dismiss him without crime is not the means to show the realm."
translations.idiomatic: To dismiss him without cause is not how to show the realm what the throne values."

sentences.zh: 乃除亦乞剌台佥宪湖南。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed Yeqilutai Surveillance Vice-Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yeqilutai was instead appointed surveillance vice-commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 文宗尝欲游西湖，自当谏曰：「陛下以万乘之尊而泛舟自乐，如天下何？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong once wished to tour West Lake; Zidang remonstrated: "Your Majesty with the honor of ten thousand chariots yet drifting in boats for personal pleasure—what of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong wished to tour West Lake, Zidang remonstrated, "Your Majesty holds the dignity of the Son of Heaven. If you drift on the lake for amusement, what will the realm think?"

sentences.zh: 不听。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 自当遂称疾不从行。

translations.literal: Zidang thereupon claimed illness and did not follow on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Zidang claimed illness and refused to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 文宗在舟中，顾谓台臣曰：「自当终不满朕此游耶？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong in the boat turned and said to censorate officials: "Does Zidang to the end not approve of this tour of mine?"
translations.idiomatic: On the boat Wenzong turned to the censors and said, "Does Zidang still disapprove of this outing of mine?"

sentences.zh: 台臣尝奏除目，文宗以笔涂一人姓名，而缀将作院官闾闾之名。

translations.literal: Censorate officials once memorialized appointment lists; Emperor Wenzong with his brush crossed out one man's name and appended the name Lü Lü, an official of the Directorate of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: When censors submitted appointment lists, Wenzong crossed out one name with his brush and added that of Lü Lü, an official of the Directorate of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 自当言：「闾闾为人诙谐，惟可任教坊司，若以居风纪，则台纲扫地矣。」

translations.literal: Zidang said: "Lü Lü is a man of jest and wit; he may only be fit to direct the Music Office. If he is placed in charge of discipline, the censorate's standards will be swept to the ground."
translations.idiomatic: Zidang said, "Lü Lü is witty and amusing and fit only for the Music Office. Put him in charge of discipline and the censorate's standards will be ruined."

sentences.zh: 文宗乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong dropped the appointment.

sentences.zh: 已而出为陕西行台侍御史。

translations.literal: Thereafter he went out as Attendant Censor of the Shaanxi Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed attendant censor of the Shaanxi regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 顺帝初，除福建都转运盐使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shundi's reign he was appointed Director-General of Salt Transport for Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shundi's reign he was appointed director-general of salt transport for Fujian.

sentences.zh: 先是，自当为左司郎中时，泰定帝尝欲以河间、江浙、福建盐引六万赐中书参议撒迪，自当执不可，仅以福建盐引二万赐之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zidang was director of the left section, Emperor Taiding once wished to grant sixty thousand salt certificates of Hejian, Jiangsu-Zhejiang, and Fujian to Secretariat Participant Sadi; Zidang held firm that it could not be done and only two ten-thousands of Fujian salt certificates were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zidang was director of the left section, Emperor Taiding wished to grant Sadi, a Secretariat participant, sixty thousand salt certificates from Hejian, Jiangsu-Zhejiang, and Fujian. Zidang objected and only twenty thousand Fujian certificates were granted.

sentences.zh: 至是，自当复建言盐引宜尽资国用以纾民力。

translations.literal: At this time Zidang again proposed that salt certificates ought entirely to fund state use to ease the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Now he again memorialized that salt certificates should go entirely to state revenue to ease the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 时撒迪方为御史大夫，不以为怨，数遣人省自当母于京师所居。

translations.literal: At that time Sadi was Grand Censor; he did not regard it as resentment and several times sent people to visit Zidang's mother at her residence in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sadi was then grand censor but bore no grudge and often sent people to visit Zidang's mother in the capital.

sentences.zh: 既而丁母忧，居间久之，复起为浙西肃政廉访使。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he mourned his mother; dwelling in retirement for a long while, he was again raised as Surveillance Commissioner of Western Zhe for Rectifying Government.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he remained in retirement for a long time, then was recalled as surveillance commissioner of Western Zhe.

sentences.zh: 时有以驸马为江浙行省丞相者，其宦竖恃公主势，坐杭州达鲁花赤位，令有司强买民间物，不从辄殴之。

translations.literal: At that time there was one made chief councillor of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang Regional Secretariat through being an imperial son-in-law; his eunuch attendants relied on the princess's power, sat in the Darughachi's seat at Hangzhou, and ordered the authorities to forcibly buy goods from common people—if they did not comply they were beaten.
translations.idiomatic: A chief councillor of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang regional secretariat was an imperial son-in-law whose eunuch attendants, relying on the princess's power, sat in the Hangzhou darughachi's seat and ordered officials to seize goods from the people by force, beating those who refused.

sentences.zh: 有司来白自当，自当即逮之械以令众，自是丞相府无敢为民害者。

translations.literal: The authorities came to report to Zidang; Zidang immediately arrested them and put them in cangues to command the multitude; from then the chief councillor's residence dared not harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: When officials reported this to Zidang, he immediately arrested the men and put them in stocks as a warning; after that the chief councillor's household dared not harm the people.

sentences.zh: 寻召为同佥枢密院事。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Associate Commissioner of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned as associate commissioner of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 寻复为治书侍御史、同知经筵事。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made Associate Censor of the Secretariat and Associate Director of Classics Lecture Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon again made associate censor of the Secretariat and associate director of classics lecture affairs.

sentences.zh: 宁夏人有告买买等谋害太师伯颜者，伯颜委自当与中书、枢密等官往宁夏鞫问，无其情，乃以诬罔坐告者罪。

translations.literal: A man of Ningxia reported that Maimai and others plotted to harm Grand Preceptor Bayan; Bayan entrusted Zidang together with Secretariat and Privy Council officials to go to Ningxia to examine and question; there was no such circumstance, and they therefore punished the accuser for false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: A Ningxia man accused Maimai and others of plotting against Grand Preceptor Bayan. Bayan sent Zidang with Secretariat and Privy Council officials to investigate; finding no truth in the charge, they punished the accuser for false accusation.

sentences.zh: 伯颜怒，自当前曰：「太师所以令吾三人勘之者，以国法所在也。

translations.literal: Bayan was angry; Zidang stepped forward and said: "The reason the Grand Preceptor ordered the three of us to examine the case is that national law stands there.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan was angry. Zidang stepped forward and said, "The Grand Preceptor sent the three of us to investigate because the law required it.

sentences.zh: 必以罪吾三人，则自当实主其事，宜独当之。」

translations.literal: If you must punish the three of us, then Zidang in fact directed the affair and ought to bear it alone."
translations.idiomatic: If you must punish someone, I directed the inquiry and should bear the blame alone."

sentences.zh: 伯颜乃左迁自当同知徽政院事。

translations.literal: Bayan thereupon demoted Zidang to Associate Administrator of the Huizheng Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan demoted Zidang to associate administrator of the Huizheng Commission.

sentences.zh: 自当历事四朝，官自从仕郎累转至通奉大夫，常衎洁在位，刚介弗回，终始一节，有古遗直之风。

translations.literal: Zidang served through four reigns; his office rose cumulatively from Junior Gentleman to Grand Master for Court Audience; he constantly maintained purity in office, was upright and unbending, one principle from beginning to end, and had the air of an ancient survivor of straight remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Zidang served four reigns, rising from junior gentleman to grand master for court audience. He remained pure in office, upright and unyielding, consistent from first to last, with the spirit of the ancient remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 然卒以是忤权贵而不复柄用，君子皆惜焉。

translations.literal: Yet in the end because of this he offended powerful nobles and was not again employed in chief posts; gentlemen all regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he finally offended the powerful and was never again given high office, to the regret of all worthy men.

sentences.zh: 阿荣，字存初，怯烈氏。

translations.literal: Arong, style name Cunchu, of the Qielie clan.
translations.idiomatic: Arong, whose style name was Cunchu, was of the Qielie clan.

sentences.zh: 父按摊，中书右丞。

translations.literal: His father Antan was Right Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Antan was right councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 阿荣幼事武宗，备宿卫，累迁官，为湖南道宣慰副使。

translations.literal: Arong in youth served Emperor Wuzong, was equipped for palace guard, rose through offices, and became Vice Commissioner of the Hunan Circuit Pacification Commission.
