translations.idiomatic: Arong served Emperor Wuzong in youth as a palace guard, rose through the ranks, and became vice commissioner of the Hunan circuit pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 温迪罕奉使宣抚湖南，事无大小，悉以委之。

translations.literal: Undihan on embassy to pacify and comfort Hunan entrusted matters great and small entirely to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Undihan was sent to pacify Hunan, he entrusted all affairs, large and small, to Arong.

sentences.zh: 会列郡岁饥，阿荣分其廪禄为粥，以食饿者，仍发粟赈之，所活甚众。

translations.literal: It happened that the various prefectures had famine that year; Arong divided his salary grain into congee to feed the hungry, and still issued grain for relief; those kept alive were very many.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the region, Arong used his salary to make gruel for the hungry and distributed grain for relief, saving many lives.

sentences.zh: 广西寇起，众皆汹惧。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Guangxi; the multitude was all in turbulent fear.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Guangxi, everyone was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 阿荣镇之以静，督有司治兵守其境，寇不敢入。

translations.literal: Arong calmed them with stillness, supervised the authorities in drilling troops to guard the borders, and the bandits did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: Arong calmed the people, organized troops to guard the border, and the bandits did not dare enter.

sentences.zh: 迁湖广行省左右司郎中，召佥会福院事，寻除吏部尚书。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Left and Right Sections of the Huguang Regional Secretariat, summoned to administer the Affairs of the Hall of Joint Blessing, and soon appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director in the Huguang regional secretariat, summoned to administer the Hall of Joint Blessing, and soon appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，出为湖南宣慰使，改浙东道宣慰使都元帅，以疾辞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding he went out as Pacification Commissioner of Hunan, was changed to Pacification Commissioner and Commander-in-Chief of the Eastern Zhe Circuit, and resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiding reign he became pacification commissioner of Hunan, then of Eastern Zhe as commander-in-chief, but resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 天历初，复起为吏部尚书，寻参议中书省事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianli he was again raised as Minister of Personnel, soon Participant in Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianli reign he was again made Minister of Personnel and soon participant in Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜中书参知政事、知经筵事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat and Director of Classics Lecture Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed associate administrator of the Central Secretariat and director of classics lecture affairs.

sentences.zh: 进奎章阁大学士、荣禄大夫、太禧宗禋院使，都典制神御殿事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion, Grand Master for Glorious Blessing, Director of the Court of Imperial Blessings and Ancestral Offerings, and overall supervisor of the Spirit Imperial Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion, grand master for glorious blessing, director of the Court of Imperial Blessings, and overall supervisor of the Spirit Imperial Hall.

sentences.zh: 文宗眷遇之甚，而阿荣亦尽心国政，知无不言。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong favored him greatly, and Arong also devoted his full heart to state affairs, speaking whatever he knew.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong favored him greatly, and Arong devoted himself to state affairs, speaking out whenever he knew something needed saying.

sentences.zh: 久之，心忽郁郁不乐，谒告南归武昌。

translations.literal: After a long while his heart suddenly grew depressed and unhappy; he requested leave and returned south to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he grew depressed, asked leave, and returned south to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 至元元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，阿荣闲居，以文翰自娱，博究前代治乱得失，见其会心者，则扼腕曰：「忠臣孝子国家之宝，为奇男子烈丈夫者固不当如是耶！」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Arong lived in retirement, he took letters and writing for amusement, broadly investigated the gains and losses of order and disorder in former ages, and when he saw what struck his heart he would clutch his wrist and say: "Loyal ministers and filial sons are the state's treasure—should extraordinary men and fierce husbands not be like this?"
translations.idiomatic: In retirement Arong amused himself with literature and studied the rise and fall of past dynasties. When something moved him he would clench his fist and say, "Loyal ministers and filial sons are the state's treasure. Should not every true man aspire to be like them?"

sentences.zh: 日与韦布之士游，所至山水佳处，鸣琴赋诗，日夕忘返。

translations.literal: Daily he traveled with men in plain cloth; wherever he reached fine landscapes of mountains and waters, he would play the zither and compose poetry, from day to evening forgetting to return.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his days with scholars in plain dress, playing the zither and composing poetry at scenic places until evening, forgetting to return home.

sentences.zh: 尤深于数学，逆推事成败利不利及人祸福寿夭贵贱，多奇中。

translations.literal: He was especially deep in numerology, retroactively deducing whether affairs would succeed or fail, profit or not profit, and people's fortune and misfortune, long life or early death, noble or base rank—many strangely hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in numerology and could predict the outcome of affairs and people's fortune, lifespan, and rank with uncanny accuracy.

sentences.zh: 天历三年春，策士于廷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Tianli the court examined scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Tianli the court held the civil examination.

sentences.zh: 阿荣与虞集会于直庐，慨然兴叹，语集曰：「更一科后科举当辍，辍两科而复，复则人材彬彬大出矣。」

translations.literal: Arong and Yu Ji met in the direct lodge; he sighed with feeling and said to Ji: "After one more round the examinations will halt; halt two rounds and then restore—when restored, talented men will emerge in splendid profusion."
translations.idiomatic: Arong met Yu Ji in the palace lodge and sighed, "After one more examination the civil service exams will be suspended. They will halt for two rounds and then resume, and when they resume talented men will emerge in great numbers."

sentences.zh: 又叹曰：「荣不复见之矣，君犹及见之。」

translations.literal: He sighed again: "Arong will not see it again; you may still see it."
translations.idiomatic: He sighed again, "I shall not live to see it, but you may."

sentences.zh: 集应曰：「得士之多，幸如存初言。

translations.literal: Ji replied: "Obtaining many scholars—fortunately it will be as Cunchu said.
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied, "If many scholars are obtained, it will be as you say, Cunchu.

sentences.zh: 今文治方兴，未必有中辍之理。

translations.literal: Now literary government is just rising; there may not necessarily be reason for a mid-way halt.
translations.idiomatic: Literary government is now flourishing; there may be no reason for a suspension.

sentences.zh: 存初国家世臣，妙于文学，以盛年登朝，在上左右，斯文属望。

translations.literal: Cunchu is a hereditary minister of the state, subtle in letters; with flourishing years he ascended court, at the ruler's left and right—the literary tradition looks to him.
translations.idiomatic: You are a hereditary minister, skilled in letters, in your prime at court beside the throne; the literary tradition looks to you.

sentences.zh: 集老且衰，见亦何补耶！」

translations.literal: Ji is old and declining—what use is there in seeing it?"
translations.idiomatic: I am old and declining—what use would my seeing it be?"

sentences.zh: 阿荣又叹曰：「数当然耳。」

translations.literal: Arong sighed again: "Numbers make it so, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Arong sighed again, "It is fate—that is all."

sentences.zh: 集问何以知之，弗答。

translations.literal: Ji asked how he knew; he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Ji asked how he knew, but he did not answer.

sentences.zh: 后三年卒。

translations.literal: Three years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died.

sentences.zh: 元统三年，科举果罢，至正元年始复，如其言。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuantong the examinations indeed halted; in the first year of Zhizheng they were first restored—as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuantong the examinations were indeed suspended, and in the first year of Zhizheng they were restored, just as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 小云石海涯

translations.literal: Xiaoyunshihaiya
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyunshihaiya

sentences.zh: 小云石海涯，家世见其祖《阿里海涯传》。

translations.literal: Xiaoyunshihaiya's family background is seen in his grandfather's biography of Alihaiya.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyunshihaiya's family background is given in the biography of his grandfather Alihaiya.

sentences.zh: 其父楚国忠惠公，名贯只哥，小云石海涯遂以贯为氏，复以酸斋自号。

translations.literal: His father was the Loyal and Beneficent Duke of Chu, named Guanzhige; Xiaoyunshihaiya thereupon took Guan as his surname and again styled himself the Sour Studio.
translations.idiomatic: His father was the Loyal and Beneficent Duke of Chu, named Guanzhige; Xiaoyunshihaiya took Guan as his surname and styled himself the Sour Studio.

sentences.zh: 母廉氏，夜梦神人授以大星使吞之，已而有妊。

translations.literal: His mother was of the Lian clan; at night she dreamed a divine man gave her a great star to swallow, and thereafter she became pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Lian clan, dreamed that a god gave her a great star to swallow, and soon after she conceived.

sentences.zh: 及生，神彩秀异。

translations.literal: When he was born, his spirit and appearance were elegant and extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At birth his bearing was remarkably fine.

sentences.zh: 年十二三，膂力绝人，使健兒驱三恶马疾驰，持槊立而待，马至，腾上之，越二而跨三，运槊生风，观者辟易。

translations.literal: At twelve or thirteen his physical strength surpassed others; he had strong youths drive three fierce horses at swift gallop, held a spear standing to wait, and when the horses arrived leaped upon them, crossing two and straddling three, wielding the spear so wind was born—viewers shrank back.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve or thirteen his strength was extraordinary. He had strong men drive three fierce horses at full gallop, stood waiting with a spear, and when they arrived leaped onto them, crossing two horses and straddling three, whirling his spear so fast the wind whistled and onlookers shrank back.

sentences.zh: 或挽强射生，逐猛兽，上下峻阪如飞，诸将咸服其趫捷。

translations.literal: Sometimes drawing the strong bow to shoot living prey, chasing fierce beasts, ascending and descending steep slopes like flight—all generals submitted to his swift agility.
translations.idiomatic: He could draw the heavy bow, hunt wild beasts, and race up and down steep slopes; all the generals admired his agility.

sentences.zh: 稍长，折节读书，目五行下。

translations.literal: When somewhat grown he restrained himself to read books, his eyes taking in five lines at once.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he turned to study and could read five lines at a glance.

sentences.zh: 吐辞为文，不蹈袭故常，其旨皆出人意表。

translations.literal: When he uttered words as literary composition he did not tread in old patterns; his purport all went beyond people's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: His writing followed no conventional pattern and always surprised readers with its meaning.

sentences.zh: 初，袭父官为两淮万户府达鲁花赤。

translations.literal: At first he inherited his father's office as Darughachi of the Two Huai Myriad Households Commission.
translations.idiomatic: At first he inherited his father's post as darughachi of the Two Huai myriad households commission.

sentences.zh: 镇永州，御军极严猛，行伍肃然。

translations.literal: Garrisoning Yong Prefecture, he controlled the army with extreme severity and fierceness; the ranks were solemn and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Stationed at Yong Prefecture, he commanded the army with great severity and kept the ranks in strict order.

sentences.zh: 稍暇，辄投壶雅歌，意所暢适，不为形迹所拘。

translations.literal: When slightly free he would play pitch-pot and sing elegant songs, following what his mind found pleasant, not constrained by formal conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare moments he played pitch-pot and sang refined songs as he pleased, unconstrained by formal propriety.

sentences.zh: 一日，呼弟忽都海涯语之曰：「吾生宦情素薄，顾祖父之爵不敢不袭，今已数年矣，愿以让弟，弟幸勿辞。」

translations.literal: One day he called his younger brother Huduhaiya and said to him: "My born inclination toward office has always been thin, yet considering my grandfather's enfeoffment I dared not fail to inherit; now it has already been several years—I wish to yield it to you, younger brother; pray do not decline."
translations.idiomatic: One day he called his younger brother Huduhaiya and said, "I have never cared much for office, but I dared not refuse my grandfather's rank. I have held it for years now and wish to yield it to you—please do not refuse."

sentences.zh: 语已，即解所绾黄金虎符佩之。

translations.literal: When the words were finished, he immediately unfastened the golden tiger tally he wore and attached it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Having spoken, he unfastened his golden tiger tally and gave it to his brother.

sentences.zh: 北从姚燧学，燧见其古文峭厉有法及歌行古乐府慷慨激烈，大奇之。

translations.literal: Going north he studied with Yao Sui; Sui saw his ancient prose stern and forceful with method, and his songs, ballads, and ancient yuefu passionate and intense—he greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: He went north to study with Yao Sui, who marveled at his stern classical prose and his passionate songs and yuefu ballads.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在东宫，闻其以爵位让弟，谓宫臣曰，「将相家子弟其有如是贤者邪！」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong in the Eastern Palace, hearing that he had yielded rank to his younger brother, said to palace officials: "Among sons and younger brothers of generals and ministers, are there such worthy men?"
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong, still heir apparent, heard that he had yielded his rank to his brother, he said to palace officials, "Can there be such worthy men among the sons of generals and ministers?"

sentences.zh: 俄选为英宗潜邸说书秀才，宿卫禁中。

translations.literal: Shortly he was selected as lecturing scholar of the hidden residence for Emperor Yingzong and kept night guard within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon chosen as lecturer at Yingzong's princely residence and served on night guard in the palace.

sentences.zh: 仁宗践祚，上疏条六事：一曰释边戍以修文德，二曰教太子以正国本，三曰设谏官以辅圣德，四曰表姓氏以旌勋胄，五曰定服色以变风俗，六曰举贤才以恢至道。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended the throne, he submitted a memorial itemizing six matters: first, release border garrisons to cultivate civil virtue; second, teach the crown prince to rectify the state's foundation; third, establish remonstrating officials to assist sagely virtue; fourth, display surnames to honor meritorious descent; fifth, fix dress colors to transform customs; sixth, raise worthy talent to restore the utmost Way.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne he memorialized six proposals: release border garrisons to cultivate civil virtue; instruct the crown prince to secure the dynastic foundation; establish remonstrating officials to assist the emperor's virtue; honor meritorious clans by displaying their surnames; fix dress colors to reform customs; and raise worthy talent to restore the highest Way.

sentences.zh: 书凡万餘言，未报。

translations.literal: The memorial in all ran to more than ten thousand words; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ran to more than ten thousand words and received no reply.

sentences.zh: 拜翰林侍读学士、中奉大夫、知制诰同修国史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Academician Reader, Grand Master for Court Audience, Drafter of Imperial Proclamations with concurrent duty revising the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin reader academician, grand master for court audience, drafter of imperial proclamations, and reviser of the national history.

sentences.zh: 会议科举事，多所建明，忽喟然叹曰：「辞尊居卑，昔贤所尚也。

translations.literal: In conference on examination affairs he proposed many enlightened measures, then suddenly sighed and said: "Declining the honored and dwelling in the humble—sages of old prized this.
translations.idiomatic: In deliberations on the civil examinations he made many proposals, then sighed and said, "To decline honor and dwell in humility is what the ancient sages prized.

sentences.zh: 今禁林清选，与所让军资孰高，人将议吾后矣。」

translations.literal: Now the pure selection of the Forbidden Grove—compared with the military funds I yielded, which is higher? People will discuss me afterward."
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin is a pure and honored post. Compared with the military command I gave up, which is higher? People will judge me by this hereafter."

sentences.zh: 乃称疾辞还江南，卖药于钱唐市中，诡姓名，易服色，人无有识之者。

translations.literal: He thereupon claimed illness, resigned, and returned to the south; he sold medicine in the Qiantang market, concealed his name, changed his dress, and no one recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed illness, resigned, and returned to the south, selling medicine in the Qiantang market under a false name and changed dress so that no one recognized him.

sentences.zh: 偶过梁山泺，见渔父织芦花为被，欲易之以。

translations.literal: By chance passing Liangshan Marsh, he saw a fisherman weaving reeds into a quilt and wished to exchange it for silk.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Liangshan Marsh he saw a fisherman weaving a reed-flower quilt and wished to trade silk for it.

sentences.zh: 渔父疑其为人，阳曰：「君欲吾被，当更赋诗。」

translations.literal: The fisherman suspected he was someone and falsely said: "If you want my quilt, you must compose another poem."
translations.idiomatic: The fisherman suspected his identity and said, "If you want my quilt, you must compose a poem."

sentences.zh: 遂援笔立成，竟持被去。

translations.literal: He thereupon took up the brush and finished on the spot, and in the end carried the quilt away.
translations.idiomatic: He took up the brush and finished a poem on the spot, then carried the quilt away.

sentences.zh: 人间喧传芦花被诗。

translations.literal: Among people the Reed-Flower Quilt poem was loudly transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Word of his Reed-Flower Quilt poem spread among the people.

sentences.zh: 其依隐玩世多类此。

translations.literal: His reclusion and playing with the world were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His reclusion and playful detachment from the world were mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 晚年为文日邃，诗亦冲淡。

translations.literal: In his later years his literary composition daily deepened, and his poetry also was mild and unadorned.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years his prose grew ever deeper and his poetry more serene.

sentences.zh: 草隶等书，稍取古人之所长，变化自成一家，所至士大夫从之若云，得其片言尺牍，如获拱璧。

translations.literal: In cursive, clerical, and other scripts he slightly took the strong points of the ancients, transformed them, and formed a school of his own; wherever he went scholars and officials followed like clouds; obtaining a fragment of his words or a foot of his writing was like obtaining a round jade disk.
translations.idiomatic: In cursive and clerical script he adapted the strengths of the ancients into a style of his own. Scholars flocked to him wherever he went, and a scrap of his writing was treasured like a jade disk.

sentences.zh: 其视死生若昼夜，绝不入念虑，攸攸若欲遗世而独立云。

translations.literal: He regarded life and death as day and night, never entering thought at all, distant as if wishing to leave the world and stand alone.
translations.idiomatic: He treated life and death as day and night, never troubling his mind, distant as if he wished to leave the world and stand alone.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年五月八日卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the fifth month of the first year of Taiding he died, age thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the eighth day of the fifth month of the first year of Taiding at the age of thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 赠集贤学士、中奉大夫、护军，追封京兆郡公，谥文靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Academician of the Jixian Hall, Grand Master for Court Audience, and Guardian General; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jingzhao Commandery; posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Jixian academician, grand master for court audience, and guardian general, enfeoffed as Duke of Jingzhao, with the posthumous title Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 有文集若干卷、《直解孝经》一卷行于世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in several scrolls and one scroll of Straight Explanation of the Classic of Filial Piety circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in several scrolls and his Straight Explanation of the Classic of Filial Piety circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 子男二人：阿思兰海牙，慈利州达鲁花赤；

translations.literal: Sons, two: Asilanhaiya, Darughachi of Cili Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Asilanhaiya, darughachi of Cili Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 次八三海涯。

translations.literal: second, Basanhaiya.
translations.idiomatic: and second, Basanhaiya.

sentences.zh: 孙女一人，有学识，能词章，归怀庆路总管段谦云。

translations.literal: Granddaughter, one: learned and able in lyric composition; she married Duan Qianyun, pacification commissioner of the Huaqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had one granddaughter, learned and skilled in poetry, who married Duan Qianyun, pacification commissioner of the Huaqing circuit.

sentences.zh: 泰不华

translations.literal: Taibuhua
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua

sentences.zh: 泰不华，字兼善，伯牙吾台氏。

translations.literal: Taibuhua, style name Jianshan, of the Bayawutai clan.
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua, whose style name was Jianshan, was of the Bayawutai clan.

sentences.zh: 初名达普化，文宗赐以今名，世居白野山。

translations.literal: His original name was Tapuhua; Emperor Wenzong granted him the present name; for generations the family dwelt at Baiye Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Tapuhua; Emperor Wenzong gave him his present name; his family had long lived at Baiye Mountain.

sentences.zh: 父塔不台，入直宿卫，历仕台州录事判官，遂居于台。

translations.literal: His father Tabutai entered direct palace guard service, passed through offices as Records Clerk and Judge at Taizhou, and thereupon settled in Tai.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tabutai served in the palace guard, held office as records clerk and judge at Taizhou, and settled there.

sentences.zh: 家贫，好读书，能记问。

translations.literal: The family was poor; he loved reading books and could remember and inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Though his family was poor, he loved reading and had a remarkable memory.

sentences.zh: 集贤待制周仁荣养而教之。

translations.literal: Jixian Academician-in-Waiting Zhou Renrong raised and taught him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Renrong, Jixian academician-in-waiting, raised and taught him.

sentences.zh: 年十七，江浙乡试第一。

translations.literal: At seventeen he placed first in the Jiangsu-Zhejiang provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he ranked first in the Jiangsu-Zhejiang provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 明年，对策大廷，赐进士及第，授集贤修撰，转秘书监著作郎，拜江南行台监察御史。

translations.literal: The next year, answering policy questions in the great court, he was granted jinshi with first honors, appointed Compiler of the Jixian Hall, transferred to Authoring Gentleman of the Palace Library, and appointed Investigating Censor of the Jiangnan Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took the palace examination, received the jinshi degree with highest honors, was appointed Jixian compiler, then authoring gentleman of the Palace Library, and investigating censor of the Jiangnan regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 时御史大夫脱欢怙势贪暴，泰不华劾罢之。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Censor Tuohuan relied on power and was greedy and violent; Taibuhua impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Censor Tuohuan abused his power with greed and violence, Taibuhua impeached him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 文宗建奎章阁学士院，擢为典签，拜中台监察御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong established the Kui Zhang Pavilion Academy, he was promoted to Proofreader and appointed Investigating Censor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong established the Kui Zhang Pavilion Academy, he was promoted to proofreader and appointed investigating censor of the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 顺帝即位，加文宗后太皇太后之号，大臣燕铁木兒、伯颜皆列地封王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shundi ascended the throne, the title Grand Empress Dowager was added to Emperor Wenzong's consort; great ministers El Temür and Bayan were all granted territories and enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shundi came to the throne, Wenzong's consort was given the title Grand Empress Dowager, and ministers El Temür and Bayan were enfeoffed as princes with territorial grants.

sentences.zh: 泰不华率同列上章言：「婶母不宜加徽称，相臣不当受王土。」

translations.literal: Taibuhua led his colleagues in submitting a memorial saying: "The aunt-by-marriage ought not receive an elevated title; chief ministers ought not receive princely lands."
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua led his colleagues in memorializing, "The aunt-by-marriage should not receive an elevated title, and chief ministers should not receive princely lands."

sentences.zh: 太后怒，欲杀言者。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was angry and wished to kill those who spoke.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was furious and wished to execute the memorialists.

sentences.zh: 泰不华语众曰：「此事自我发之，甘受诛戮，决不敢累诸公也。」

translations.literal: Taibuhua said to the multitude: "This matter began from me; I willingly accept execution— I absolutely dare not implicate you gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua told the others, "This began with me. I am willing to die and will never implicate you."

sentences.zh: 已而太后怒解曰：「风宪有臣如此，岂不能守祖宗之法乎？」

translations.literal: Before long the empress dowager's anger dissolved and she said: "The censorate has such a minister—how could it fail to preserve the laws of the ancestors?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long the empress dowager's anger passed and she said, "With such censors, how could the ancestral laws fail to be preserved?"

sentences.zh: 赐金币二，以旌其直。

translations.literal: She granted two gold coins to honor his uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: She rewarded him with gold to honor his integrity.

sentences.zh: 出佥河南廉访司事，俄移淮西。

translations.literal: He went out to administer the affairs of the Henan Surveillance Commission, soon transferred to Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to administer the Henan surveillance commission and soon transferred to Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 继迁江南行御史臺经历，辞不赴，转江浙行省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: He was next transferred to Administrator of the Jiangnan Regional Censorate, declined and did not take up the post, and was changed to Director of the Left and Right Sections of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was next appointed administrator of the Jiangnan regional censorate but declined, and was made director in the Jiangsu-Zhejiang regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 浙西大水害稼，会泰不华入朝，力言于中书，免其租。

translations.literal: Western Zhe suffered great flood damage to crops; when Taibuhua entered court he spoke forcefully to the Central Secretariat and their rent was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: When a great flood ruined the crops of Western Zhe, Taibuhua memorialized the Secretariat on entering court and secured remission of their rent.

sentences.zh: 擢秘书监，改礼部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to the Palace Library and changed to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to superintendent of the Palace Library and then vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 至正元年，除绍兴路总管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Shaoxing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizheng he was appointed pacification commissioner of the Shaoxing circuit.

sentences.zh: 革吏弊，除没官牛租，令民自实田以均赋役。

translations.literal: He reformed clerical abuses, abolished rent on confiscated official oxen, and ordered the people to report their own fields truthfully to equalize taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: He reformed clerical abuses, abolished rent on confiscated official cattle, and required people to declare their land honestly so taxes and corvée could be assessed fairly.

sentences.zh: 行乡饮酒礼，教民兴让，越俗大化。

translations.literal: He carried out the village drinking ceremony, taught the people to promote yielding, and Yue customs were greatly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: He instituted the village drinking ceremony, taught the people courtesy and deference, and greatly reformed local customs.

sentences.zh: 召入史馆，与修辽、宋、金三史，书成，授秘书卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned into the History Office to help compile the histories of Liao, Song, and Jin; when the books were completed he was appointed Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the History Office to help compile the histories of Liao, Song, and Jin, and when the work was finished was appointed director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 升礼部尚书，兼会同馆事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Rites and concurrently administered the affairs of the Hall of Joint Assembly.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Rites and concurrently administered the Hall of Joint Assembly.

sentences.zh: 黄河决，奉诏以珪玉白马致祭河神。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River burst its banks, he received an edict to offer sacrifice to the River God with jade scepter and white horse.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River burst its banks, he was ordered to sacrifice to the River God with jade and a white horse.

sentences.zh: 竣事上言：「淮安以东，河入海处，宜仿宋置撩清夫，用辊江龙铁扫，撼荡沙泥，随潮入海。」

translations.literal: When the affair was concluded he submitted words: "East of Huai'an, where the river enters the sea, one ought to imitate the Song in establishing dredging laborers, using iron sweeps like rolling river dragons to shake and move sand and mud, following the tide into the sea."
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed he memorialized, "East of Huai'an, where the river enters the sea, the Song practice of dredging crews using iron river-drags to stir sand and mud out to sea with the tide should be restored."

sentences.zh: 朝廷从其言，会用夫屯田，其事中废。

translations.literal: The court followed his words, but when corvée labor was used for garrison farming the affair was abandoned midway.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his proposal, but when labor was diverted to garrison farming the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 八年，台州黄岩民方国珍为蔡乱头、王伏之仇逼，遂入海为乱，劫掠漕运粮，执海道千户德流于实。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Fang Guozhen of Huangyan in Taizhou, pressed by enmity with Cai Luantou and Wang Fuzhi, went to sea in rebellion, plundered grain transport tribute, and seized Maritime Route Chiliarch Deliu Zishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Fang Guozhen of Huangyan in Taizhou, driven by feud with Cai Luantou and Wang Fuzhi, took to the sea in rebellion, plundered grain transport, and seized maritime route chiliarch Deliu Zishi.

sentences.zh: 事闻，诏江浙参政朵兒只班总舟师捕之。

translations.literal: When the matter was heard, an edict ordered Jiangsu-Zhejiang Associate Administrator Duozhiban to command the fleet to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Duozhiban, associate administrator of Jiangsu-Zhejiang, was ordered to command a fleet against him.

sentences.zh: 追至福州五虎门，国珍知事危，焚舟将遁，官军自相惊溃，朵兒只班遂被执。

translations.literal: Pursuing to the Wuhumen of Fuzhou, Fang Guozhen knew the affair was perilous, burned his boats and was about to flee; government troops in mutual alarm collapsed, and Duozhiban was thereupon seized.
translations.idiomatic: Pursued to Wuhumen at Fuzhou, Fang Guozhen burned his boats to flee; the government fleet panicked and collapsed, and Duozhiban was captured.

sentences.zh: 国珍迫其上招降之状，朝廷从之，国珍兄弟皆授之以官，国珍不肯赴，势益暴横。

translations.literal: Fang Guozhen forced him to submit a memorial of surrender; the court followed it and the Fang brothers were all granted offices, but Fang Guozhen would not attend and his power grew ever more violent and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guozhen forced him to submit a surrender memorial; the court accepted it and enfeoffed the Fang brothers, but Fang Guozhen refused to attend court and grew more violent.

sentences.zh: 九年，诏泰不华察实以闻，既得其状，遂上招捕之策，不听。

translations.literal: In the ninth year an edict ordered Taibuhua to investigate the truth and report; once he obtained the circumstances, he submitted a plan to summon and capture them, but it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Taibuhua was ordered to investigate and report; learning the truth, he proposed a plan to capture Fang Guozhen, but the court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 寻除江东廉访使，改翰林侍读学士、知制诰同修国史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangdong, changed to Hanlin Academician Reader, Drafter of Imperial Proclamations with concurrent duty revising the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made surveillance commissioner of Jiangdong, then Hanlin reader academician, drafter of imperial proclamations, and reviser of the national history.

sentences.zh: 已而出为都水庸田使。

translations.literal: Thereafter he went out as Commissioner of Waterworks and Garrison Farming.
translations.idiomatic: He then left the capital as commissioner of waterworks and garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 十年十二月，国珍复入海，烧掠沿海州郡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the tenth year Fang Guozhen again went to sea, burning and plundering coastal prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the tenth year Fang Guozhen again took to the sea and raided coastal prefectures.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月，诏孛罗帖木兒为江浙行省左丞，总兵至庆元。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year an edict appointed Boluotiemu'er Left Councillor of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang Regional Secretariat, commanding troops to Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eleventh year Boluotiemu'er was appointed left councillor of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang regional secretariat and led troops to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 以泰不华谂知贼情状，迁浙东道宣慰使都元帅，分兵于温州，使夹攻之。

translations.literal: Because Taibuhua understood the bandits' circumstances, he was transferred to Pacification Commissioner and Commander-in-Chief of the Eastern Zhe Circuit, dividing troops at Wenzhou to make a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: Because Taibuhua understood the rebels, he was made pacification commissioner and commander-in-chief of Eastern Zhe, with troops at Wenzhou to attack from both sides.

sentences.zh: 未几，国珍寇温，泰不华纵火筏焚之，一夕遁去。

translations.literal: Before long Fang Guozhen raided Wen; Taibuhua sent fire rafts to burn them, and in one night they fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fang Guozhen raided Wenzhou; Taibuhua sent fire rafts against him and the rebels fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 既而孛罗帖木兒密与泰不华约以六月乙未合兵进讨。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Boluotiemu'er secretly agreed with Taibuhua to unite troops on the yiwei day of the sixth month for a joint advance and punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Boluotiemu'er then secretly agreed with Taibuhua to join forces on the yiwei day of the sixth month for a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 孛罗帖木兒乃以壬辰先期至大闾洋，国珍夜率劲卒纵火鼓噪，官军不战皆溃，赴水死者过半。

translations.literal: Boluotiemu'er thereupon on the renchen day arrived early at Dalüyang; Fang Guozhen by night led crack troops to set fires and raise clamor; government troops collapsed without fighting, and more than half who entered the water died.
translations.idiomatic: Boluotiemu'er arrived early at Dalüyang on the renchen day; Fang Guozhen led crack troops by night to set fires and raise a din, and the government army collapsed without fighting—more than half drowned.

sentences.zh: 孛罗帖木兒被执，反为国珍饰辞上闻。

translations.literal: Boluotiemu'er was seized and instead ornamented words for Fang Guozhen to report upward.
translations.idiomatic: Boluotiemu'er was captured and instead sent Fang Guozhen's embellished report to the court.

sentences.zh: 泰不华闻之痛愤，辍食数日。

translations.literal: When Taibuhua heard he was pained and indignant and stopped eating for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua was grief-stricken and angry and stopped eating for days.

sentences.zh: 朝廷弗之知，复遣大司农达识帖木迩等至黄岩招之。

translations.literal: The court did not know of it and again sent Grand Commission for Agriculture Dashitiemuer and others to Huangyan to summon them.
translations.idiomatic: The court, unaware of the truth, again sent Grand Commission for Agriculture Dashitiemuer to Huangyan to negotiate surrender.

sentences.zh: 国珍兄弟皆登岸罗拜，退止民间小楼。

translations.literal: The Fang brothers all came ashore and bowed in array, then withdrew to a small building among the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Fang brothers came ashore and bowed in ceremony, then withdrew to a small house among the people.

sentences.zh: 是夕，中秋月明，泰不华欲命壮士袭杀之，达识帖木迩适夜过泰不华，密以事白之，达识帖木迩曰：「我受诏招降耳，公欲擅命耶？」

translations.literal: That evening, on the bright moon of Mid-Autumn Festival, Taibuhua wished to order stalwart men to strike and kill them; Dashitiemuer happened to pass Taibuhua by night and secretly informed him of the affair; Dashitiemuer said: "I received an edict to summon surrender—does the lord wish to act on private authority?"
translations.idiomatic: That Mid-Autumn night, under a bright moon, Taibuhua wished to send brave men to kill them. Dashitiemuer happened to pass by and, told of the plan, said, "I was ordered to accept surrender. Do you wish to act on your own authority?"

sentences.zh: 事乃止。

translations.literal: The affair was thereupon halted.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 檄泰不华亲至海滨，散其徒众，拘其海舟兵器，国珍兄弟复授官有差。

translations.literal: An order was sent that Taibuhua personally come to the seashore, disperse their followers, detain their sea boats and weapons, and the Fang brothers were again granted offices of varying rank.
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua was ordered to the coast to disperse Fang's followers and seize his ships and weapons; the Fang brothers were again granted offices.

sentences.zh: 既而迁泰不华台州路达鲁花赤。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Taibuhua was transferred to Darughachi of the Taizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua was soon transferred to darughachi of the Taizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 十二年，朝廷征徐州，命江浙省臣募舟师守大江，国珍怀疑，复入海以叛。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the court campaigned against Xuzhou and ordered Jiangsu-Zhejiang provincial ministers to recruit a fleet to guard the Great River; Fang Guozhen grew suspicious and again went to sea in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when the court campaigned against Xuzhou and ordered Jiangsu-Zhejiang to recruit a fleet for the Yangzi, Fang Guozhen grew suspicious and rebelled at sea again.

sentences.zh: 泰不华自分以死报国，发兵扼黄岩之澄江，而遣义士王大用抵国珍，示约信，使之来归。

translations.literal: Taibuhua resolved in himself to die repaying the state; he raised troops to block Chengjing River at Huangyan and sent the righteous man Wang Dayong to reach Fang Guozhen, showing covenant faith to make him come and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua resolved to die for his country, deployed troops to hold Chengjing River at Huangyan, and sent the loyalist Wang Dayong to Fang Guozhen with pledges of good faith to induce his surrender.

sentences.zh: 国珍益疑，拘大用不遣，以小舸二百突海门，入州港，犯马鞍诸山。

translations.literal: Fang Guozhen grew more suspicious, detained Dayong and would not release him, and with two hundred small boats burst through Haimen, entered the prefectural harbor, and attacked the mountains of Ma'an and others.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guozhen grew more suspicious, detained Wang Dayong, and with two hundred small boats burst through Haimen into the harbor and attacked the Ma'an hills.

sentences.zh: 泰不华语众曰：「吾以书生登显要，诚虑负所学。

translations.literal: Taibuhua said to the multitude: "I as a scholar ascended to prominence—I truly fear failing what I have learned.
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua told his men, "I rose from scholarship to high office and fear I may fail what I have learned.

sentences.zh: 今守海隅，贼甫招徠，又复为变，君辈助我击之，其克则汝众功也，不克则我尽死以报国耳。」

translations.literal: Now guarding the sea corner, the bandits were just summoned and again rebel—gentlemen, help me strike them; if we overcome, it is your collective merit; if we do not overcome, I will all die repaying the state."
translations.idiomatic: Now guarding this coast, the rebels were just offered surrender and rebel again. Help me strike them. If we win, the credit is yours; if we lose, I will die repaying my country."

sentences.zh: 众皆踊跃愿行。

translations.literal: The multitude all eagerly wished to go.
translations.idiomatic: All eagerly volunteered.

sentences.zh: 时国珍戚党陈仲达往来计议，陈其可降状。

translations.literal: At that time Fang Guozhen's kinsman Chen Zhongda came and went in deliberation, stating his condition of possible surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's kinsman Chen Zhongda came and went negotiating and reported that surrender was possible.

sentences.zh: 泰不华率部众，张受降旗乘潮而前。

translations.literal: Taibuhua led his troops, raised the surrender-acceptance banner, and advanced on the tide.
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua led his troops forward under a surrender banner, riding the tide.

sentences.zh: 船触沙不能行，垂与国珍遇，呼仲达申前议，促达目动气索，泰不华觉其心异，手斩之。

translations.literal: The boats struck sand and could not proceed; almost meeting Fang Guozhen, he called Zhongda to renew the former deliberation; Zhongda's eyes moved and his breath was tight—Taibuhua perceived his heart was different and with his hand cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: The boats grounded on sand; as he was about to meet Fang Guozhen he called Chen Zhongda to renew the talks. Seeing Zhongda's shifting eyes and strained manner, Taibuhua sensed treachery and killed him with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 即前搏贼船，射死五人，贼跃入船，复斫死二人，贼举槊来刺，辄斫折之。

translations.literal: He immediately advanced to grapple the rebel boats, shot dead five men; rebels leaped into the boat and he again cut down two; rebels raised spears to stab and he always cut and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: He charged the rebel boats, shot five men dead, cut down two more who leaped aboard, and broke every spear thrust at him.

sentences.zh: 贼群至，欲抱持过国珍船，泰不华嗔目叱之，脱起，夺贼刀，又杀二人。

translations.literal: Rebels came in a crowd wishing to seize and carry him to Fang Guozhen's boat; Taibuhua glared and shouted at them, broke free and rose, seized a rebel sword, and killed two more.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels swarmed to drag him to Fang's boat, he glared and shouted them off, broke free, seized a rebel sword, and killed two more.

sentences.zh: 贼攒槊刺之，中颈死，犹植立不仆，投其尸海中。

translations.literal: Rebels massed spears and stabbed him; struck in the neck he died, yet still stood planted without falling; they cast his corpse into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels stabbed him with massed spears; struck in the neck he died yet remained standing until they cast his body into the sea.

sentences.zh: 年四十九。

translations.literal: Age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-nine years old.

sentences.zh: 时十二年三月庚子也。

translations.literal: It was the gengzi day of the third month of the twelfth year.
translations.idiomatic: It was the gengzi day of the third month of the twelfth year.

sentences.zh: 僮名抱琴，及临海尉李辅德、千户赤盏、义士张君璧皆死之。

translations.literal: His servant named Baoqin, and Linhai Commandant Li Fude, Chiliarch Chizan, and the righteous man Zhang Junbi all died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His servant Baoqin, Linhai commandant Li Fude, chiliarch Chizan, and the loyalist Zhang Junbi all died with him.

sentences.zh: 泰不华既没，除江浙行省参知政事，行台州路达鲁花赤事，不及闻命已。

translations.literal: After Taibuhua had perished, he was appointed Associate Administrator of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang Regional Secretariat, performing the affairs of Darughachi of the Taizhou Circuit—he did not live to hear the order.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed associate administrator of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang regional secretariat and acting darughachi of Taizhou, but never heard the order.

sentences.zh: 后三年，追赠荣禄大夫、江浙行省平章政事、柱国，封魏国公，谥忠介，立庙台州，赐额崇节。

translations.literal: Three years later he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Glorious Blessing, Pacification Commissioner of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang Regional Secretariat, and Pillar of the State; enfeoffed as Duke of Wei; posthumous title Zhongjie; a temple was established at Taizhou with the plaque title Honoring Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was posthumously made grand master for glorious blessing, pacification commissioner of Jiangsu-Zhejiang, and pillar of the state, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with the posthumous title Zhongjie; a temple was built at Taizhou with the plaque Honoring Integrity.

sentences.zh: 泰不华尚气节，不随俗浮沉。

translations.literal: Taibuhua prized integrity and did not drift with the vulgar current.
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua prized integrity and would not drift with the times.

sentences.zh: 太平为台臣劾去相位，泰不华独饯送都门外。

translations.literal: Taiping was impeached by censorate ministers and removed from chief ministerial rank; Taibuhua alone saw him off with a farewell feast outside the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping was impeached and removed from the chief ministership, Taibuhua alone saw him off outside the capital gate.

sentences.zh: 太平曰：「公且止，勿以我累公。」

translations.literal: Taiping said: "Sir, stop—do not let me implicate you."
translations.idiomatic: Taiping said, "Stop, sir—do not let me bring trouble on you."

sentences.zh: 泰不华曰：「士为知己死，宁畏祸耶！」

translations.literal: Taibuhua said: "A gentleman dies for one who knows him—would he fear disaster?"
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua said, "A gentleman dies for one who knows him. Why should I fear disaster?"

sentences.zh: 后虽为时相摈斥，人莫不韪之。

translations.literal: Later, though he was rejected by the chief ministers of the time, no one failed to approve him.
translations.idiomatic: Though later chief ministers ostracized him, everyone approved his conduct.

sentences.zh: 善篆隶，温润遒劲。

translations.literal: He was skilled in seal and clerical script—mild, moist, forceful, and vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at seal and clerical script, writing in a mild yet forceful hand.

sentences.zh: 尝重类《复古编》十卷，考正讹字，于经史多有据云。

translations.literal: He once reclassified the ten scrolls of the Compilation for Restoring Antiquity, examining and correcting erroneous characters, with much basis in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He re-edited the ten-scroll Compilation for Restoring Antiquity, correcting erroneous characters with solid grounding in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 餘阙，字廷心，一字天心，唐兀氏，世家河西武威。

translations.literal: Yu Que, style name Tingxin, another style name Tianxin, of the Tangwu clan, a hereditary family of Wuwei in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Que, whose style names were Tingxin and Tianxin, was of the Tangwu clan, a family long established at Wuwei in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 父沙剌臧卜，官庐州，遂为庐州人。

translations.literal: His father Shalazangbu held office at Luzhou and thereupon became a man of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shalazangbu served at Luzhou, and the family became Luzhou natives.

sentences.zh: 少丧父，授徒以养母，与吴澄弟子张恆游，文学日进。

translations.literal: He lost his father young, taught pupils to support his mother, traveled with Zhang Heng, disciple of Wu Cheng, and his letters and learning daily advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he taught pupils to support his mother, studied with Zhang Heng, a disciple of Wu Cheng, and steadily improved in letters.

sentences.zh: 元统元年，赐进士及第，授同知泗州事，为政严明，宿吏皆惮之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was granted jinshi with first honors and appointed Associate Administrator of Sizhou; his government was stern and bright, and old clerks all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuantong he received the jinshi degree with highest honors and was appointed associate administrator of Sizhou; his stern administration made veteran clerks fear him.

sentences.zh: 俄召入，应奉翰林文字，转中书刑部主事。

translations.literal: Shortly he was summoned in as Attendant-in-Waiting for Hanlin Documents and transferred to Chief Clerk of the Punishments Section of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned as Hanlin attendant-in-waiting and transferred to chief clerk in the Secretariat's punishments section.

sentences.zh: 以不阿权贵，弃官归。

translations.literal: Because he did not flatter powerful nobles, he abandoned office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Refusing to flatter the powerful, he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 寻以修辽、金、宋三史召，复入翰林，为修撰。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to compile the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song, again entered the Hanlin, and became Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to help compile the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song, re-entered the Hanlin, and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 拜监察御史，改中书礼部员外郎，出为湖广行省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor, changed to Vice Director of the Rites Section of the Central Secretariat, and went out as Director of the Left and Right Sections of the Huguang Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor, then vice director in the Secretariat's rites section, and then director in the Huguang regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 会莫徭蛮反，右丞沙班当帅师，坚不往，无敢让之者。

translations.literal: It happened that the Moyao tribes rebelled; Right Councillor Shaban ought to command the army but firmly would not go, and none dared reprove him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Moyao tribes rebelled, Right Councillor Shaban was to command the army but refused to go, and no one dared reprove him.

sentences.zh: 阙曰：「右丞当往，受天子命为方岳重臣，不思执弓矢讨贼，乃欲自逸邪！

translations.literal: Que said: "The right councillor ought to go. Receiving the Son of Heaven's command as a weighty minister of a region, he does not think to take bow and arrow to punish rebels—does he wish to indulge himself?
translations.idiomatic: Que said, "The right councillor must go. Appointed by the Son of Heaven as a regional minister, he should take up arms against rebels instead of seeking ease.

sentences.zh: 右丞当往。」

translations.literal: The right councillor ought to go."
translations.idiomatic: The right councillor must go."

sentences.zh: 沙班曰：「郎中语固是，如刍饷不足何？」

translations.literal: Shaban said: "The director's words are indeed correct—but what if fodder and provisions are insufficient?"
translations.idiomatic: Shaban said, "You are right, director—but what if fodder and provisions are insufficient?"

sentences.zh: 阙曰：「右丞第往，此不难致也。」

translations.literal: Que said: "The right councillor need only go—this is not hard to obtain."
translations.idiomatic: Que said, "Go, and that will not be hard to obtain."

sentences.zh: 阙下令趣之，三日皆集，沙班行。

translations.literal: Que issued orders to hurry them; in three days all were gathered, and Shaban marched.
translations.idiomatic: Que ordered supplies rushed; within three days all was gathered and Shaban marched.

sentences.zh: 复以集贤经历召入。

translations.literal: He was again summoned in as Administrator of the Jixian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was again summoned as Jixian administrator.

sentences.zh: 迁翰林待制。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin academician-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 出佥浙东道廉访司事。

translations.literal: He went out to administer the affairs of the Eastern Zhe Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to administer the Eastern Zhe surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 丁母忧，归庐州。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother and returned to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he returned to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 盗起河南，陷郡县。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Henan and seized prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose in Henan and seized prefectures and districts.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，行中书于淮东，改宣慰司为都元帅府，治淮西，起阙副使、佥都元帅府事，分兵守安庆。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng a mobile Secretariat was established in Huaidong; the Pacification Commission was changed to a Commandery-in-Chief's Office governing Huaixi; Que was raised as Vice Commissioner and Administrator of the Commandery-in-Chief's Office, dividing troops to guard Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng a mobile Secretariat was set up in Huaidong, the pacification commission was made a commandery-in-chief's office governing Huaixi, and Que was recalled as vice commissioner to divide troops and defend Anqing.

sentences.zh: 于时南北音问隔绝，兵食俱乏，抵官十日而寇至，拒却之。

translations.literal: At that time north and south were cut off from news; troops and food were both scarce; ten days after reaching office bandits arrived and he repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: North and south were cut off from communication; troops and food were scarce. Ten days after he took office bandits arrived and he repelled them.

sentences.zh: 乃集有司与诸将议屯田战守计，环境筑堡寨，选精甲外捍，而耕稼于中。

translations.literal: He thereupon gathered responsible officials and generals to deliberate on garrison farming and plans for war and defense, built fortresses and stockades around the perimeter, selected crack armor for external defense, and farmed within.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered officials and generals to plan garrison farming and defense, built fortresses around the perimeter, posted crack troops on the outside, and farmed within.

sentences.zh: 属县灊山八社，土壤沃饶，悉以为屯。

translations.literal: In the subordinate district, the eight communities of Qianshan had rich fertile soil and all were made garrison farms.
translations.idiomatic: The eight communities of Qianshan in the subordinate district had rich soil and were all turned into garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 明年，春夏大饥，人相食，乃捐俸为粥以食之，得活者甚众。

translations.literal: The next year, in spring and summer there was great famine and people ate one another; he donated his salary to make congee to feed them, and those kept alive were very many.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring and summer brought terrible famine and cannibalism; he donated his salary for gruel and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 民失业者数万，咸安集之。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of people who lost their livelihoods were all settled and gathered.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled tens of thousands who had lost their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 请于中书，得钞三万锭以赈民。

translations.literal: He requested from the Central Secretariat and obtained thirty thousand strings of paper money to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: He obtained thirty thousand strings of paper money from the Secretariat for relief.

sentences.zh: 升同知、副元帅。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Associate Administrator and Vice Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to associate administrator and vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 又明年秋，大旱，为文祈灊山神，三日雨，岁以不饥。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the year after next there was great drought; he composed a text praying to the god of Qianshan; after three days rain fell and the year was without famine.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn brought severe drought; he prayed to the god of Qianshan, rain fell after three days, and the year passed without famine.

sentences.zh: 盗方据石荡湖，出兵平之，令民取湖鱼而输鱼租。

translations.literal: Bandits were just occupying Shidang Lake; he sent troops to pacify them and ordered the people to take fish from the lake and pay fish rent.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops to pacify bandits occupying Shidang Lake and levied a fish tax on the lake's catch.

sentences.zh: 十五年夏，大雨，江涨，屯田禾半没，城下水涌，有物吼声如雷，阙祠以少牢，水辄缩。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifteenth year great rain fell, the river rose, half the garrison farm grain was submerged, water surged below the city, and there was a thing roaring like thunder; Que sacrificed to it with a young ox and a pig, and the water immediately receded.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifteenth year heavy rains swelled the river, half the garrison crops were flooded, water surged below the walls with a thunderous roar; Que sacrificed with a young ox and pig, and the water receded.

sentences.zh: 秋稼登，得粮三万斛。

translations.literal: The autumn harvest was abundant and thirty thousand hu of grain were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn harvest yielded thirty thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 阙度军有餘力，乃浚隍增陴，隍外环以大防，深堑三重，南引江水注之，环植木为栅，城上四面起飞楼，表里完固。

translations.literal: Que judged the army had surplus strength and thereupon dredged the moat and raised the parapet; outside the moat he ringed a great dike, three layers of deep trenches, drew river water from the south to fill them, planted trees in a ring as palisades, and raised flying towers on all four sides atop the wall—inside and outside completely secure.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the army had spare strength, he deepened the moat, raised the walls, built triple ditches and a great outer dike, channeled river water into them, planted palisades, and erected flying towers on all sides until the defenses were complete.

sentences.zh: 俄升都元帅。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted to Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 广西猫军五万从元帅阿思兰沿江下抵庐州，阙移文谓苗蛮不当使之窥中国，诏阿思兰还军。

translations.literal: Fifty thousand Miao troops of Guangxi followed Marshal Asilan down the river to Luzhou; Que sent a dispatch saying the Miao tribes ought not be allowed to peer into China; an edict ordered Asilan to return the army.
translations.idiomatic: When fifty thousand Guangxi Miao troops under Marshal Asilan reached Luzhou by river, Que protested that barbarian troops should not be allowed to enter China; the court ordered Asilan to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 猫军有暴于境者，即收杀之，凛凛莫敢犯。

translations.literal: When Miao troops committed violence within the borders he immediately seized and killed them; in awe none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately executed any Miao troops who committed violence in his territory, and none dared offend him.

sentences.zh: 时群盗环布四外，阙居其中，左提右挈，屹为淮一保障。

translations.literal: At that time bandit groups were spread in a ring on all four sides; Que dwelt in the midst, lifting left and drawing right, standing firm as the one bulwark of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: With bandits surrounding him on all sides, Que held the center and stood firm as the sole bulwark of the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 论功，拜江淮行省参知政事，仍守安庆，通道于江右，商旅四集。

translations.literal: Discussing merit, he was appointed Associate Administrator of the Jianghuai Regional Secretariat, still guarding Anqing; a passage was opened to Jiangyou and merchants and travelers gathered from the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made associate administrator of the Jianghuai regional secretariat while still defending Anqing; he opened communications to Jiangyou and merchants flocked in.

sentences.zh: 池州赵普胜帅众攻城，连战三日败去。

translations.literal: Zhao Pusheng of Chizhou led a multitude to attack the city; after three days of continuous battle he was defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pusheng of Chizhou besieged the city for three days and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 未几又至，相拒二旬始退，怀宁县达鲁花赤伯家奴战死。

translations.literal: Before long he came again; they resisted each other twenty days before he withdrew; the Darughachi of Huaining County, Bojianu, died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He returned soon after and was held off for twenty days; Bojianu, darughachi of Huaining, was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 十七年，赵普胜同青军两道攻我，拒战一月餘，竟败而走。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Zhao Pusheng together with the Green Army attacked on two routes; resisting battle for more than a month, they were at last defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Zhao Pusheng and the Green Army attacked on two fronts; after more than a month of fighting they were defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 秋，拜淮南行省左丞。

translations.literal: In autumn he was appointed Left Councillor of the Huainan Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he was appointed left councillor of the Huainan regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 安庆倚小孤山为籓蔽，命义兵元帅胡伯颜统水军戍焉。

translations.literal: Anqing relied on Little Gushan Mountain as a screen and barrier; he ordered Righteous Army Marshal Hu Boyan to command the water army to garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing relied on Little Gushan as a screen; he ordered righteous-army marshal Hu Boyan to garrison the water force there.

sentences.zh: 十月，沔阳陈友谅自上游直捣小孤山，伯颜与战四日夜不胜，急趣安庆。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Chen Youliang of Mianyang from upstream drove straight at Little Gushan Mountain; Boyan fought four days and nights without victory and urgently hastened to Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Chen Youliang of Mianyang attacked Little Gushan from upstream; Boyan fought four days and nights without victory and hurried to Anqing.

sentences.zh: 贼追至山口镇，明日癸亥，遂薄城下。

translations.literal: The bandits pursued to Shankou Town; the next day, guihai, they thereupon pressed close below the city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pursued to Shankou Town, and on the guihai day the next day pressed up to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 阙遣兵扼于观音桥。

translations.literal: Que sent troops to block at Guanyin Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Que sent troops to hold Guanyin Bridge.

sentences.zh: 俄饶州祝寇攻西门，阙斩却之。

translations.literal: Shortly Zhu Kou of Raozhou attacked the west gate and Que cut them down and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhu Kou of Raozhou attacked the west gate; Que defeated and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，贼乘东门，红旗登城，阙简死士力击，贼复败去。

translations.literal: On yisi the bandits seized the east gate; red banners mounted the wall; Que selected death-dedicated warriors and struck with force; the bandits were again defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the rebels stormed the east gate and raised red banners on the wall; Que chose elite warriors and drove them back again.

sentences.zh: 戊申，贼并军攻东西二门，又却之。

translations.literal: On wushen the bandits united their armies to attack the east and west gates and were again repelled.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the rebels combined forces against the east and west gates and were repelled again.

sentences.zh: 贼恚甚，乃树栅起飞楼。

translations.literal: The bandits were extremely enraged and thereupon erected palisades and raised flying towers.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, the rebels built palisades and raised siege towers.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，复来攻我，金鼓声震地。

translations.literal: On gengxu they again came to attack us; the sound of bells and drums shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu they attacked again, the din of drums and gongs shaking the ground.

sentences.zh: 阙分诸将各以兵捍贼，昼夜不得息。

translations.literal: Que divided the generals, each with troops to resist the bandits; day and night they could not rest.
translations.idiomatic: Que assigned each general troops to hold off the rebels; day and night they had no rest.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，贼益生兵攻东门。

translations.literal: On guimao the bandits further increased troops to attack the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the rebels sent more troops against the east gate.

sentences.zh: 丙午，普胜军东门，友谅军西门，祝寇军南门，群盗四面蚁集，外无一甲之援。

translations.literal: On bingwu Pusheng's army at the east gate, Youliang's army at the west gate, Zhu Kou's army at the south gate—bandit groups swarmed like ants on all four sides; outside there was not the aid of a single suit of armor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Pusheng attacked the east gate, Youliang the west, Zhu Kou the south; rebels swarmed on every side and not a single ally came to their aid.

sentences.zh: 西门势尤急，阙身当之，徒步提戈为士卒先。

translations.literal: The west gate's situation was especially urgent; Que personally faced it, on foot raising his halberd to lead the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The west gate was hardest pressed; Que faced it in person, on foot with halberd in hand leading his men.

sentences.zh: 士卒号哭止之，挥戈愈力，仍分麾下将督三门之兵，自以孤军血战，斩首无算，而阙亦被十餘创。

translations.literal: Soldiers wailed and wept to stop him; he waved his halberd with still greater force, still divided generals under his command to supervise the troops at the three gates, himself with an isolated army fighting in blood—heads cut off beyond counting—yet Que also received more than ten wounds.
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers wept and tried to hold him back, but he fought all the harder, assigning generals to the other gates while he alone led a desperate battle, killing countless enemies and taking more than ten wounds himself.

sentences.zh: 日中城陷，城中火起，阙知不可为，引刀自刭，堕清水塘中。

translations.literal: At midday the city fell; fire rose within the city; Que knew nothing could be done, drew his sword and cut his own throat, and fell into Qingshui Pond.
translations.idiomatic: At midday the city fell and fires broke out within. Knowing all was lost, Que drew his sword and cut his throat, falling into Qingshui Pond.

sentences.zh: 阙妻耶卜氏及子德生、女福童皆赴井死。

translations.literal: Que's wife Lady Yebu, his son Desheng, and his daughter Futong all went to wells and died.
translations.idiomatic: Que's wife Lady Yebu, his son Desheng, and his daughter Futong all threw themselves into wells and died.

sentences.zh: 同时死者，守臣韩建一家被害，建方卧疾，骂贼不屈，贼执之以去，不知所终。

translations.literal: Those who died at the same time included the defending minister Han Jian's whole household, murdered; Jian was just then bedridden with illness, cursed the bandits and would not yield; the bandits seized him and took him away—to this day his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who died at the same time was the defending official Han Jian's entire household. Jian lay ill in bed, cursed the rebels and refused to submit; they seized him and carried him away, and his fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 城中民相率登城楼，自捐其梯曰：「宁俱死此，誓不从贼。」

translations.literal: The people within the city together climbed the city tower, themselves removing the ladders and saying: "Better all die here—we swear not to follow the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople climbed the city towers, pulled up the ladders, and declared, "We would rather all die here than submit to the rebels."

sentences.zh: 焚死者以千计。

translations.literal: Those who died by burning were counted in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died by fire numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 其知名者，万户李宗可、纪守仁、陈彬、金承宗，元帅府都事帖木补化，万户府经历段桂芳，千户火失不花、新李、卢廷玉、葛延龄、丘卺、许元琰，奏差兀都蛮，百户黄寅孙，安庆推官黄秃伦歹，经历杨恆，知事餘中，怀宁尹陈巨济，凡十八人。

translations.literal: Among the well-known were: Myriad Household Li Zongke, Ji Shouren, Chen Bin, Jin Chengzong; Commandery-in-Chief's Office Director Temubuqa; Myriad Households Office Administrator Duan Guifang; Chiliarchs Huoshibuhua, Xin Li, Lu Tingyu, Ge Yanling, Qiu Ji, Xu Yuanyan; Memorial Envoy Wuduman; Centurion Huang Yinsun; Anqing Investigating Official Huang Tulundai; Administrator Yang Heng; Clerk Yu Zhong; Huaining Magistrate Chen Juji—in all eighteen men.
translations.idiomatic: Among the well-known dead were myriad household officers Li Zongke, Ji Shouren, Chen Bin, and Jin Chengzong; commandery-in-chief office director Temubuqa; myriad households administrator Duan Guifang; chiliarchs Huoshibuhua, Xin Li, Lu Tingyu, Ge Yanling, Qiu Ji, and Xu Yuanyan; memorial envoy Wuduman; centurion Huang Yinsun; Anqing investigating official Huang Tulundai; administrator Yang Heng; clerk Yu Zhong; and Huaining magistrate Chen Juji—eighteen men in all.

sentences.zh: 其城陷之日，则至正十八年正月丙午也。

translations.literal: The day the city fell was the bingwu day of the first month of the eighteenth year of Zhizheng.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell on the bingwu day of the first month of the eighteenth year of Zhizheng.

sentences.zh: 阙号令严信，与下同甘苦，然稍有违令，即斩以徇。

translations.literal: Que's orders were stern and trusted; he shared bitterness and sweetness with those below, yet if there was the slightest violation of orders, he immediately beheaded to display.
translations.idiomatic: Que's commands were strict and trusted; he shared hardship with his men, yet the slightest disobedience was punished by immediate execution.

sentences.zh: 阙尝病不视事，将士皆吁天求以身代，阙闻，强衣冠而出。

translations.literal: Que once was ill and did not attend to affairs; officers and soldiers all cried to Heaven asking to substitute their bodies for his; when Que heard, he forced himself into cap and robes and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Que was ill and could not attend to affairs, his officers prayed Heaven to accept their lives in his stead; hearing this, he forced himself to dress and go out.

sentences.zh: 当出战，矢石乱下如雨，士以盾蔽阙，阙却之曰：「汝辈亦有命，何蔽我为！」

translations.literal: When about to go out to battle, arrows and stones fell in disorder like rain; soldiers used shields to screen Que; Que pushed them away and said: "You gentlemen also have lives—why screen me!"
translations.idiomatic: Going into battle, arrows and stones fell like rain; his men tried to shield him with their shields, but he pushed them away and said, "You have lives too—why shield me?"

sentences.zh: 故人争用命。

translations.literal: Therefore men competed to give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: His men therefore fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 稍暇，即注《周易》，帅诸生谒郡学会讲，立军士门外以听，使知尊君亲上之义，有古良将风烈。

translations.literal: When slightly free he would annotate the Book of Changes, lead the students to visit the prefectural school for joint lecture, and station soldiers outside the gate to listen, making them know the meaning of honoring the ruler and revering superiors—he had the wind and fierceness of ancient worthy generals.
translations.idiomatic: In spare moments he annotated the Book of Changes, led students to lectures at the prefectural school, and posted soldiers outside to listen, teaching them to honor ruler and superiors—the spirit of the great generals of old.

sentences.zh: 或欲挽阙入翰林，阙以国步危蹙，辞不往，其忠国之心，盖素定也。

translations.literal: Some wished to draw Que into the Hanlin; Que because the state's step was perilously cramped declined and did not go—his heart loyal to the state had long been settled.
translations.idiomatic: Some wished to bring him into the Hanlin, but Que declined because the dynasty was in peril; his loyalty to the state had long been settled.

sentences.zh: 卒时年五十六。

translations.literal: When he died he was age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 事闻，赠阙摅诚守正清忠谅节功臣、荣禄大夫、淮南江北等处行中书省平章政事、柱国，追封豳国公，谥忠宣。

translations.literal: When the matter was heard, Que was posthumously granted Meritorious Minister Who Displays Sincerity, Upholds Rectitude, and Displays Pure Loyalty, Faith, and Integrity; Grand Master for Glorious Blessing; Pacification Commissioner of the Mobile Secretariat of Huainan, Jiangbei, and Other Places; and Pillar of the State; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Bin; posthumous title Zhongxuan.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Que was posthumously made meritorious minister, grand master for glorious blessing, pacification commissioner of the Huainan and Jiangbei mobile secretariat, and pillar of the state, enfeoffed as Duke of Bin with the posthumous title Zhongxuan.

sentences.zh: 议者谓自兵兴以来，死节之臣，阙与褚不华为第一云。

translations.literal: Discussants said that since troops arose, among ministers who died for integrity, Que and Chu Buhua were the first.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that since the wars began, Que and Chu Buhua ranked first among those who died for their integrity.

sentences.zh: 阙留意经术，《五经》皆有传注。

translations.literal: Que paid attention to classical learning; on the Five Classics he all had transmitted commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Que devoted himself to classical learning and wrote commentaries on all Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 为文有气魄，能达其所欲言。

translations.literal: In literary composition he had spirit and force and could reach what he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: His prose had force and clarity and always conveyed his meaning.

sentences.zh: 时体尚江左，高视鲍、谢，徐、庾以下不论也。

translations.literal: The style of the time prized the Jiangzuo region; he looked down from a height on Bao and Xie—Xu, Yu, and those below were not discussed.
translations.idiomatic: When the fashion favored Jiangzuo poets, he held Bao Zhao and Xie Lingyun in highest regard and dismissed Xu Ling, Yu Xin, and those who came after.

sentences.zh: 篆隶亦古雅可传。

translations.literal: His seal and clerical script were also ancient and elegant, fit to be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: His seal and clerical script were also ancient and elegant, worthy of transmission.

sentences.zh: 初，阙既死，贼义之，求尸塘中，具棺敛葬于西门外。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Que had died, the bandits honored his righteousness, sought his corpse in the pond, prepared a coffin, laid him out, and buried him outside the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: After Que's death the rebels honored his integrity, recovered his body from the pond, coffined it, and buried him outside the west gate.

sentences.zh: 及安庆内附，大明皇帝嘉阙之忠，诏立庙于忠节坊，命有司岁时致祭云。

translations.literal: When Anqing submitted inward, the Great Ming emperor praised Que's loyalty, issued an edict to establish a temple at the Loyal Integrity Archway, and ordered the authorities to offer sacrifice at the seasons—thus it is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: When Anqing submitted to the Ming, the emperor praised Que's loyalty, ordered a temple built at the Loyal Integrity Archway, and commanded seasonal sacrifices by the local authorities.
